item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-22

Issues: 415 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-22 01:08 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-22

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity maintenance phase with 415 issues and 500 PRs updated in the last 24 hours, though no new releases shipped. The activity split is balanced between triage (297 open/active issues, 118 closed) and integration (294 open PRs, 206 merged/closed), indicating a healthy merge pipeline rather than a backlog stall. However, the issue queue is dominated by P0/P1 stability regressions — gateway memory blowups, update/rollback failures, and plugin lifecycle races — several of which are multi-version-old and still unresolved. The most-discussed issue (#160959, 85 comments) concerns a Gateway event-loop block introduced in 2026.9.6, suggesting the project is still absorbing the cost of its plugin-generation architecture. Overall: high engagement, strong throughput, but elevated stability debt that warrants release-blocker attention.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. The most recent stable line referenced across issues is 2026.11.3, with 2026.11.5 in beta/candidate validation (see #200606, #197083). No changelog or migration notes to report today.

3. Project Progress

206 PRs were merged or closed in the last 24h. Notable closures and advances:

  • #203368 [CLOSED] — fix(ui): skip archive exit animations outside the sidebar viewport (link): fixes a 32px row-jump artifact when archiving off-screen session groups.
  • #203346 [CLOSED] — improve: show complete 30-day Usage reports sooner (link): reduces partial-total latency and removes a 400ms preset delay.
  • #203356 [CLOSED] — fix: keep one model's cooldown deadline off other models (link): prevents provider-wide cooldown bleed from cached catalogs.
  • #199155 [CLOSED] — transcript row visibility race between CLI message send and the gateway session actor (link) — a session-state correctness fix.
  • #185578 [CLOSED] — gateway heap floor ratchet (~25 MiB/h leak) (link) — a meaningful memory-stability win.
  • Android refactor series by vincentkoc (#202892, #202898, #202903, #202876, #202877) advanced test-fixture ownership and state-consolidation work under umbrella issue #202818.

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Signal
#160959 — Gateway blocks minutes capturing large external plugins (P0, 2026.9.6 regression) 85 Highest engagement. External/workspace plugin package trees block the event loop at startup and on model-runtime republish. Maintainer review requested; no fix PR.
#191944 — macOS gateway stop/stop --force fail with "Process ancestry could not be fully inspected" 38 Native macOS service-inspection gap; UX friction on a core lifecycle command.
#197083 — Post-install Doctor WAL verification leaves 11.3 update partially finalized (P0) 32 Managed-upgrade integrity risk; state-migrated-no-rollback traps users mid-update.
#182891 — Prompt cache never reused (cache read dropped N -> 0) 22 Cost pain. Envelope rewrites and runtimeContextCarrier changes invalidate cache every request — directly hits token spend.
#200606 — 2026.11.5 candidate Doctor blocks update with plugin migration conflict 19 Release-candidate validation blocker; changed=[] mismatch.

Underlying needs: Users are primarily demanding predictable upgrades (rollback safety, Doctor honesty), lifecycle reliability (stop/start/restart across macOS/Windows), and cost transparency (prompt-cache reuse, memory ceilings). The plugin-generation architecture is the recurring fault line.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

P0 / Release-blockers

  • #160959 — Gateway event-loop block for minutes on large external plugins (regression, no fix PR). Top stability risk.
  • #197083 — Post-install WAL verification leaves 11.3 update partially finalized; external plugins stranded.
  • #169844 — Windows Control UI Gateway update hangs at "Activating," leaves Scheduled Task disabled and gateway stopped (link).

P1

  • #181432 — Baseline RSS ~1.9 GB and SQLite transaction timeouts in 2026.10.5 (Linux ARM64) (link).
  • #169797 — Gateway 2026.9.9/2026.10.1 uses ~2.5× memory of 2026.9.4 on single-CPU hosts; 3–5× slower start (link).
  • #196199 — Native Codex helper completions fail to resume parent, pausing goals and locking users out (link).
  • #197515 — Codex "data/settings upgrade is unfinished" persists on 2026.11.3; merged fix #186506 not in release (link).
  • #191476 — Matrix room stuck on "Plugin matrix consumer is closed" after image_generate race (link).
  • #153899 — Gateway drain waits full TimeoutStopSec; timers fire against closed resources (link).

P2 (selected)

  • #200756 — Windows beta.2→beta.4 update fails at package-swap (baseline package scan failed).
  • #200224 — 2026.11.5 beta refuses retired agents.defaults.heartbeat, but removing it re-enables heartbeats — a no-win migration trap.
  • #202001 — Prompt cache invalidated by system prompt section churn (openai-completions); misdiagnosed as history rewrite.
  • #136405 — memory_search hangs 15s on stalled remote embedding; no per-call timeout/retry config.

Fix-PR status: Several closed today (#199155, #185578, #203356), but the P0s (#160959, #197083, #169844) have no fix PR and are flagged needs-maintainer-review. The release-notes gap in #197515 (merged fix not shipped) is a process smell worth flagging.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #163739 — Make Control UI Ctrl+Shift+A (Archive) configurable; collides with browser shortcuts (closed as stale, product decision pending).
  • #187264 — Caller-scoped, same-conversation scheduling for non-owner channel requests (security review needed).
  • #116052 — MCP OAuth pre-registered clients (authorization_code) for servers without DCR — likely to land given growing MCP adoption.
  • #170997 — CJK bigram tokenizer for memory FTS (trigram yields 0 matches for 2-char Chinese queries).
  • #138990 — Enforceable checkpoints and bounded yields for long foreground WebChat runs.
  • #155137 — Optional Perplexity Agent API research tool.
  • #191580 (PR) — Configurable count of recent messages kept on automatic session reset.

Prediction: The MCP OAuth pre-registration (#116052) and session-reset message count (#191580) are the most shippable near-term; the CJK tokenizer (#170997) has a clear technical fix and a linked PR open. The Control UI shortcut remap (#163739) is a low-effort win that keeps getting deferred.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Upgrade anxiety — multiple users describe updates leaving installs in partial states (state-migrated-no-rollback, baseline package scan failed, WAL verification failures). Trust in the managed-update path is eroding.
  • Cost leakage — prompt-cache invalidation (#182891, #202001, #177506) is a recurring theme; users are measuring token drops in the millions and want deterministic cache reuse.
  • Memory bloat — 1.9 GB baseline RSS and 2.5× regressions on single-CPU hosts make OpenClaw feel heavy for small deployments.
  • Platform friction — macOS stop failures and Windows update hangs are blocking basic lifecycle operations.

Satisfaction signals: High comment volume with constructive diagnostics (users posting worker_turn_tool_authorities, cache-read telemetry, package-scan logs) indicates an engaged, technically sophisticated user base willing to help triage. The rapid closure of session-state and memory-leak bugs today shows responsiveness where maintainers have bandwidth.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or high-impact items needing maintainer attention:

  • #160959 — P0, 85 comments, created 2026-09-29, still open with no fix PR. The single largest stability liability.
  • #136405 — memory_search 15s hang, open since 2026-09-02, no fix PR; affects active-memory recall reliability.
  • #124306 — Exec approval card doesn't flag mount-point targets before rm -rf; open since 2026-08-15, security/UX gap.
  • #130247 — Cron jobs have no --until/--max-runs end conditions; open since 2026-08-26.
  • #116052 — MCP OAuth pre-registered clients; open since 2026-07-29, security review flagged.
  • #129388 — Context-pressure-aware continuation PR (XL, open since 2026-08-25) — long-running design that could reshape agent turn management if merged.
  • #197515 — Process gap: merged fix #186506 not present in 2026.11.3 release; needs release-train verification.

Health assessment: Throughput is strong and the community is highly engaged, but the concentration of P0/P1 stability issues in the update and plugin-lifecycle paths — combined with at least one confirmed case of a merged fix not shipping (#197515) — suggests the release pipeline needs a stability-focused pass before the next stable cut. The 2026.11.5 candidate Doctor conflicts (#200606, #200224) are immediate release-train blockers.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Data window: 2026-11-22 (24h) | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape is bifurcating into a high-velocity core (OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw) and a long-tail periphery (IronClaw, QwenPaw) where maintainer bandwidth, not contribution, is the binding constraint. Across all five projects, the dominant engineering themes are stability of the update/lifecycle path, agent security scoping (credentials, cost ceilings, permissions), and cost transparency (prompt-cache reuse, per-hop spend enforcement). Terminal integration, MCP extensibility, and multi-channel parity are emerging as table-stakes feature surfaces rather than differentiators. The ecosystem is visibly transitioning from "does the agent work?" to "can operators trust it in production?" — with upgrade safety, least-privilege design, and deterministic cost behavior now the primary competitive axes.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Release Status Health Score
OpenClaw 415 (297 open / 118 closed) 500 (294 open / 206 merged-closed) None; 2026.11.3 stable, 2026.11.5 RC ⚠️ Stressed — high throughput, elevated P0/P1 debt, release-train blockers
Hermes Agent 50 (42 open / 8 closed) 50 (35 open / 15 merged-closed) None; between cuts 🟡 Pressured but stable — strong closures, unpatched P2s, v0.23.1 regressions
IronClaw 1 (1 open / 0 closed) 0 None 🟢 Idle / nominal — single community FR, no bugs, zero PR throughput
QwenPaw 6 (4 open / 2 closed) 11 (11 open / 0 merged) None 🟠 Review-constrained — healthy inflow, zero merges, multi-month-old PRs
ZeroClaw 18 (active) 50 (43 open / 7 merged-closed) None; v0.9.1 in prep 🟢 Solid but review-bound — 7 closures incl. S1/S2 fixes, XL PR queue

Throughput ratio (PRs merged/closed per 100 updated): OpenClaw ~41, ZeroClaw ~14, Hermes ~30, QwenPaw 0, IronClaw 0.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Scale advantage is decisive. OpenClaw processes roughly 8–10× the issue and PR volume of its nearest peer (Hermes) in the same window, and ~40× ZeroClaw's daily merge count. Its community is not merely larger but technically deeper — users submit worker_turn_tool_authorities diagnostics, cache-read telemetry, and package-scan logs, effectively acting as a distributed triage force.

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Integration velocity: 206 merged/closed PRs in 24h versus single digits for peers — the only project with a genuinely industrial merge pipeline.
  • Feature breadth: MCP OAuth, Android refactor series, Control UI, multi-provider cooldown isolation, usage analytics — areas peers are only beginning to scope.
  • Community infrastructure: sustained 85-comment threads and multi-version regression tracking imply institutional memory peers lack.

Technical approach differences: OpenClaw has committed to a plugin-generation architecture with a managed-update + Doctor verification pipeline. This is the source of both its power (extensibility) and its pain (event-loop blocking on large plugin trees, WAL verification failures, rollback traps). Hermes and ZeroClaw favor asset/config-driven extensibility (providers.json, WASM plugins) that trades depth for predictability.

Community size comparison: OpenClaw = far larger, more mature, and more demanding. Its weakness is stability debt proportional to its surface area — the same complexity that drives adoption drives P0 concentration in update/lifecycle paths (#160959, #197083, #169844).

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

The following requirements surfaced independently across multiple projects, indicating ecosystem-level demand:

Theme Projects Specific Need
Update / lifecycle reliability OpenClaw (#197083, #169844), Hermes (#152519, #145469), ZeroClaw (Windows CI) Predictable upgrades, rollback safety, honest Doctor/verification; no partial-finalize traps
Cost enforcement & transparency OpenClaw (#182891, #202001 — prompt-cache invalidation), ZeroClaw (#12626, #12627, #12628 — per-hop ceilings, route_down non-functional) Hard cost guarantees; documented settings that actually work
Least-privilege / scoped credentials ZeroClaw (RFC #12422), OpenClaw (#187264 caller-scoped scheduling), Hermes (#157803 trusted input) Agent acts on services without exposing secrets to the model
Cross-platform gaps (Windows/macOS) OpenClaw (macOS stop, Windows update hang), Hermes (#152435, #143567 — ≥4 Windows bugs), ZeroClaw (#12484 Windows plugin) Consistent lifecycle/process management; reduced platform CI blind spots
Terminal integration / agent status Hermes (OSC 7501, 5 PRs), OpenClaw (usage reports, session reset) Machine-readable agent state (idle/working/blocked/error)
Provider catalog expansion IronClaw (#8174 LLMTR), OpenClaw (#116052 MCP OAuth), Hermes (#156806 reasoning effort) Zero-code, OpenAI-compatible gateway onboarding
Silent-failure elimination Hermes (#156806, #137357, #89587), QwenPaw (#8851, #8848), ZeroClaw (#9896) Visible, honest state; no no-op buttons or misleading banners

Signal strength: Update reliability and cost enforcement appear in 3 of 5 projects with severity ≥P1/S2 — these are the ecosystem's shared failure modes.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent IronClaw QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Feature focus Full-stack platform: UI, gateway, Android, plugins, MCP Terminal/TUI + gateway, proactivity roadmap Minimal catalog-driven LLM provider Channel-native agent (WeChat, console) Security-hardened runtime, multi-channel
Target users Power users, plugin developers, enterprise ops Developers, desktop interactivity users Integrators wanting simple provider swap Multi-channel/community operators Multi-tenant operators, cost-sensitive enterprises
Architecture Plugin-generation + managed update pipeline Gateway + SessionState refactor + OSC status protocol providers.json asset catalog Console + plugin routes + runtime base-path WASM plugins + IRC/Twitch extraction to registry
Distinctive bet Depth/feature breadth Desktop UX contract + terminal parity Simplicity & low surface area Channel parity & async completion Least-privilege security model
Primary weakness Stability debt in update path Cross-platform erosion Idle / low activity Review bottleneck XL PR review queue

Key insight: No two projects compete directly. OpenClaw is the platform, Hermes the developer terminal tool, ZeroClaw the security/cost guardian, QwenPaw the channel integrator, IronClaw the minimalist provider host. Overlap is increasing at the edges (MCP, cost, provider catalogs), which will pressure differentiation in 2027.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers:

  • Tier 1 — Industrial-scale (OpenClaw): 415 issues + 500 PRs/24h. Mature, heavily engaged, but carrying systemic stability debt. Momentum high; trust eroding in managed-update path.
  • Tier 2 — Rapid iteration (Hermes, ZeroClaw): 50 issues + 50 PRs each. Both actively closing S1/S2 bugs and landing features (OSC 7501, cost fixes), but review bandwidth is visibly the constraint (XL backlogs, needs-author-action PRs).
  • Tier 3 — Stabilizing / constrained (QwenPaw): Healthy issue quality, zero merges in 24h, PRs open 1–2+ months. At risk of contributor attrition.
  • Tier 4 — Idle (IronClaw): Single community FR, no PR throughput, no bugs. Stable but dormant — monitoring warranted.

Trajectory:

  • Iterating fastest: Hermes (salvage-train PR consolidation), ZeroClaw (security hardening + cost cluster).
  • Stabilizing / batch-releasing: OpenClaw (absorbing plugin-arch cost), ZeroClaw (v0.9.1 prep + deslop tracker).
  • At risk: QwenPaw (review bottleneck), IronClaw (momentum stall).

Maturity proxy: OpenClaw ≈ production platform with operational debt. Hermes/ZeroClaw ≈ post-1.0 products in hardening. QwenPaw/IronClaw ≈ early-to-mid projects with process gaps.

7. Trend Signals

Extracted from cross-project community feedback — actionable for AI agent developers:

  1. Trust is the new feature. Users across projects measure trust via outcomes: upgrades that complete, cost limits that hold, buttons that work. No-op Steer buttons (Hermes #141973), non-functional route_down (ZeroClaw #12626), and misleading docs that wipe env vars (QwenPaw #8843) all erode confidence faster than missing features lose adoption. Design implication: treat honesty of state and config as a first-class requirement, not polish.

  2. Cost control must be hierarchical and unforgeable. OpenClaw's prompt-cache invalidation and ZeroClaw's per-hop ceiling bypass (#12627) reveal that cost logic fails under multi-agent delegation and envelope mutation. Developers should: make ceilings inheritable and non-bypassable at spawn time, and make cache reuse deterministic rather than incidental.

  3. Least-privilege agent credentials are the emerging security primitive. ZeroClaw's RFC #12422 (agent acts without seeing the credential) is the clearest articulation of a need echoed in OpenClaw (#187264) and Hermes (#157803). Expect "scoped, revocable, model-invisible" credentials to become a standard pattern.

  4. Platform coverage is a silent quality tax. Windows and macOS generated independent bug clusters in OpenClaw, Hermes, and ZeroClaw. Teams shipping cross-platform should treat Windows/Fedora CI parity as a release gate, not an afterthought.

  5. Terminal-native agent status (OSC 7501-style) is standardizing. Hermes' 5-PR salvage train shows demand for machine-readable agent state from the terminal. Value for developers: enables external orchestration/monitoring without API polling — a composability win.

  6. Provider catalogs want zero-code extensibility. Request patterns (IronClaw LLMTR, OpenClaw MCP OAuth) favor asset-driven configuration over adapter code. Build for config, not code, when onboarding gateways.

  7. Review bandwidth is the ecosystem's scarcest resource. In four of five projects, open PRs outnumber merges decisively, and multi-month-old XL PRs appear in QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, and Hermes. Developers contributing upstream should submit small, issue-linked PRs with filled templates — matching the pattern of today's fast-closed fixes.

Bottom line for decision-makers: The ecosystem is healthy in aggregate but unevenly stressed. OpenClaw leads on scale and must now pay down stability debt before its next cut. Hermes and ZeroClaw are the strongest hardening stories, both gated by review capacity. QwenPaw and IronClaw need maintainer attention to avoid momentum loss. Across all, the winning differentiator in 2027 will be demonstrable trust — reliable upgrades, enforceable costs, and provable least-privilege — rather than raw feature count.

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-22

Generated: 2026-11-22 01:08 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — 2026-11-22

1. Ecosystem Overview

Today's digests show a landscape consolidating around a single new architecture family — Inkling 2 (Thinking Machines Lab) — with every layer of the stack racing to land support simultaneously: vLLM (Ampere/Ada gating), llama.cpp (DSpark speculation, tensor split, FA bias), Ollama (blocked on a LLAMA_CPP_VERSION bump), and Unsloth (LoRA/QLoRA training). No project shipped a stable release in the last 24h; activity is concentrated in PR queues and issue triage. The dominant risk theme is correctness under load — silent output corruption, cross-request leaks, and NaN perplexity — rather than raw throughput. Meanwhile, quantization format churn (vLLM's Marlin→Humming migration, Kitty 2-bit KV cache) and Blackwell SM120 stability signal that the hardware/format matrix is still settling. Gateway and disaggregation integration (vllm.Render gRPC, P/D bootstrap_room) is maturing but exposes multi-tenant isolation gaps.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Layer Issues (active/tracked) PRs (active/in-flight) Release Status (24h)
vLLM Serving engine ~10 top-severity bugs; 3 new WIP trackers ~8 in-flight (kernels, gRPC, quant) No release
SGLang Serving engine 10 ranked regressions; 1.0 tracker active ~6 open (AMD kernels, JIT bench) No release (1.0 tracker)
llama.cpp Local runtime ~16 ranked issues; 2 critical ~7 open (Inkling 2, FA bias, Vulkan) b12611–b12622 (12 builds)
Ollama Local runtime ~6 ranked; parser cluster ~6 open (VRAM, parser, shards) No release
LiteLLM Gateway ~10 ranked; redaction stack ~10 open (redaction 5-PR split) v1.112.0-dev.2 + v1.108.15 LTS
Unsloth Fine-tuning ~11 ranked; 2 open blockers ~10 open/closed (memory, GRPO) No release

Read: llama.cpp is the only project shipping continuously (12 builds in 24h) — consistent with its release cadence model. LiteLLM is the only project with a formal LTS line, now a moving pointer. vLLM and SGLang are in "queue-heavy, release-quiet" mode, typical of pre-release hardening (SGLang 1.0) and format migration (vLLM Marlin→Humming).

3. Model Support Race

Inkling 2 is the contested frontier. Support status by layer:

Layer Project Status
Serving vLLM Ampere/Ada gating PR (#69165) — Triton path reuse
Serving SGLang No explicit Inkling 2 entry today (AMD Kimi-K3 focus)
Local runtime llama.cpp Most advanced: DSpark speculator (#32218), tensor split (#32751), FA bias (#32740); but NaN perplexity on CUDA (#32710) blocks production
Local runtime Ollama Blocked — unknown arch inkling2_loop; needs LLAMA_CPP_VERSION bump from b12257 (Nov 10) to b12622
Fine-tuning Unsloth LoRA/QLoRA training PR (#18812) landing, but inference-side GGUF load broken in Studio (#18757)

Who's ahead: llama.cpp on raw capability breadth (speculation, tensor split, FA bias), but its correctness bug makes it unusable for Inkling 2 on CUDA. vLLM is the most deployable path for serving (gated to Ampere/Ada with existing Triton paths). Unsloth is ahead on the training side but its inference path is broken. No project offers a production-safe Inkling 2 story today — this is a genuine ecosystem-wide gap.

Other notable model support: llama.cpp landed Kyutai Hibiki real-time duplex (#12619), MiniCPM5 MoE, Nemotron 3.6 Academia; vLLM added Mamba2 NVFP4 via Marlin and 2-bit KV cache; SGLang focused on AMD Kimi-K3/K2.5 kernel fusion; LiteLLM closed Gemini Live Avatar and OpenAI Skills API routing; Unsloth added AsyncGRPO tree packing for Qwen3.5/3.6 hybrids.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort is concentrated in five distinct arenas, with clear project specialization:

KV cache (highest strategic attention):

  • vLLM: 2-bit "Kitty" KV quantization (#68945), DP8 vs TP8 for MLA (7.7× KV capacity, 3.4× faster 1M-context TTFT at c=8 on 8×B200), KV offload re-queue stall (#62532), and view re-derivation waste (#64572).
  • SGLang: hybrid-GDN speculative state memory blowup (#51175), prefill CUDA graph memory starvation (#40094).
  • llama.cpp: Qwen3.8 hybrid GDN decode collapse past 80K (#27623).

Quantization (format churn):

  • vLLM: Marlin→Humming migration (full format set), NVFP4 Mamba2 via Marlin, CUTLASS int8 gating fix.
  • llama.cpp: SYCL IQ4 reorder, AVX-512 IQ3_S/IQ2_S kernels.
  • Unsloth: auto fp8 base for DiT LoRA on sm89+ (open PR), int8 CUTLASS race cache fix.

Kernels (hardware-specific):

  • SGLang: AMD Kimi-K3 perf series — fused MLA value projection + MXFP4 quant, Quark FP8 KDA, AITER MoE sort.
  • llama.cpp: SYCL fused ADD+RMS_NORM+MUL, Vulkan RDNA4 MMVQ, FA coopmat1 driver workaround.
  • vLLM: batch-invariant Qwen3-30B FP8 MoE tuning on Blackwell, FA2 split-KV decode.

Distributed serving:

  • vLLM: DP8 vs TP8 MLA benchmark is the most actionable data point today.
  • SGLang: custom all-reduce peer mapping (#52173), P/D disaggregation correctness.
  • llama.cpp: speculative decode split-mode regressions (layer vs tensor).

Batching/scheduling:

  • vLLM: --long-prefill-token-threshold behavior change (#60476) — operators must re-validate latency isolation.
  • SGLang: JIT kernel regression tracking (#52132) with per-PR baselines.

Read: vLLM owns the KV cache + quantization frontier; SGLang owns AMD/ROCm kernel fusion; llama.cpp owns CPU/SYCL/Vulkan edge kernels; Unsloth owns training memory pressure (8× video dedup, shard-streamed save, GRPO tail cut).

5. Layer Positioning

Layer Project Primary job Key differentiator today
Serving engine vLLM High-throughput, multi-hardware inference Broadest format/hardware matrix; gateway integration via vllm.Render gRPC; Rust frontend parity
Serving engine SGLang Latency-optimized serving + P/D disaggregation 1.0 stability push; AMD/ROCm kernel depth; strict config validation
Local runtime llama.cpp Portable edge/desktop inference Hardware breadth (CPU/SYCL/Vulkan/Metal/CUDA); fastest release cadence; Inkling 2 capability leader
Local runtime Ollama User-friendly local model management Easiest UX; parser correctness surface; cloud routing
Gateway LiteLLM Multi-provider routing, billing, observability LTS line; signed Docker images; redaction/privacy hardening; provider translation breadth
Fine-tuning Unsloth LoRA/QLoRA/GRPO training + Studio Memory-efficient training; vLLM speculative config passthrough; Studio as inference+training UI

Key architectural observation: the boundaries are blurring. vLLM is building a gateway integration surface (vllm.Render gRPC for llm-d sidecars) — traditionally LiteLLM's territory. Unsloth is passing speculative decoding config to vLLM (#18764) — training tooling now configures serving. Ollama wraps llama.cpp but is now gated by its version pin. Infrastructure engineers should expect to manage 3–4 of these together, not one.

6. Trend Signals

1. Correctness is the new bottleneck, not throughput. Every project surfaced a silent-correctness bug today: vLLM's HF3FS KV connector treating failed loads as cache hits (#69058) and Kimi-K3 CUDA graph silent corruption at batch=1 (#52531); SGLang's P/D cross-request output leak with HTTP 200 (#51980); llama.cpp's NaN perplexity (#32710); Ollama's parser truncating thinking mid-sentence (#19829); LiteLLM's MCP tool re-execution on retry (#43153); Unsloth's RoPE scaling silently unscaled past 8192 (#18818). Watch: add end-to-end output validation to CI; don't trust scheduler-side success signals.

2. Blackwell (SM120) is not production-ready across the stack. vLLM (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode collapse, NVFP4 wedges), SGLang (no model runs out-of-box on CUDA 13 wheel), llama.cpp (Inkling 2 IQ4_NL prefill crashes on RTX 5090), Unsloth (RDNA4 QLoRA illegal memory access). Watch: if you're targeting RTX PRO 6000/5090/consumer Blackwell, validate per-model before committing.

3. Quantization format churn is a version-pinning imperative. vLLM's Marlin→Humming migration will deprecate Marlin-backed configs; Kitty 2-bit KV cache is WIP; llama.cpp's b12622 removed internal w_s/_s overloads breaking forks; Unsloth's Q5_K_M export rejected by bundled llama.cpp build 12588. Watch: pin vLLM and llama.cpp versions; re-validate quantized deployments on upgrade; don't track main.

4. Multi-tenant isolation is under-tested. SGLang's P/D bootstrap_room leak (#51980) and vLLM's HF3FS silent-failure (#69058) are both multi-tenant correctness risks. Watch: if you run disaggregated or KV-offloaded serving in multi-tenant settings, add request-isolation tests.

5. Long-context + hybrid architectures expose memory cliffs. Qwen3.8 hybrid GDN decode collapse past 80K (#27623), hybrid-GDN speculative state blowup (#51175), MLX prefix cache eviction past 64K (#19819). Watch: size context caps conservatively on hybrid models; benchmark before defaulting to 1M-context claims.

6. Agent/application developers should watch:

  • Parser correctness (Ollama #18288, #18624, #17564; LiteLLM #48401) — truncated tool calls and leaked thinking tags are partial-token-boundary bugs, not model quality.
  • Gateway-side cost attribution (LiteLLM #53419, #53394, #46059) — client-cancelled streaming and watsonx undercounting distort spend.
  • Speculative decoding as first-class config (Unsloth #18764 → vLLM; llama.cpp DSpark 80 vs 47.6 tok/s at long context) — worth revisiting for 16 GB-card deployments.
  • Rust frontend / gRPC gateway paths (vLLM #44280, #65503) — relevant if you front vLLM with llm-d or do tokenization outside the engine.

Bottom line for decision-makers: the stack is mid-transition — format migration (vLLM), 1.0 hardening (SGLang), version-pin gating (Ollama), and LTS pointer drift (LiteLLM) all demand version pinning and re-validation discipline this cycle. The Inkling 2 race is real but no layer is production-safe yet. Prioritize correctness validation over throughput benchmarking in your next upgrade.

Per-Project Reports

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM Digest — 2026-11-22

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases in the last 24h, but the issue/PR queue is active across three fronts: SM120 (Blackwell) CUDA graph and NVFP4 stability problems continue to generate the highest-severity bug reports (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode throughput, ModelOpt NVFP4 wedges under sustained load), while quantization kernel migration progresses — the Marlin→Humming tracker is now open and a 2-bit "Kitty" KV-cache quantization PR is in WIP. On the infrastructure side, the Rust frontend feature-parity roadmap (#44280) and the vllm.Render gRPC gateway work (#65503, #67652) signal continued investment in gateway/sidecar integration and non-Python serving paths.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

No new releases in the last 24h. Relevant in-flight changes worth tracking:

  • Marlin → Humming kernel migration (#65560, RFC/tracker): Humming now covers the full format set Marlin serves (INT4/INT8 GPTQ/AWQ, FP8, MXFP8, MXFP4, NVFP4, MXFP6, INT8/FP8 activations) for dense and MoE layers. Marlin is an SM80-era kernel with no Hopper/Blackwell-specific paths. Expect eventual deprecation of Marlin-backed configs — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65560
  • --long-prefill-token-threshold behavior change since v0.31.0 (#60476): short requests behind a long prefill are no longer protected due to the lone-request exemption from #57951. Operators relying on this flag for latency isolation should re-validate — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60476

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Ampere/Ada support for Inkling 2 family (#69165, PR): Inkling2ForConditionalGeneration and Inkling2LoopForConditionalGeneration gated to run on SM80/SM86/SM89, reusing the existing Triton paths from Hopper/SM12x — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69165
  • 2-bit KV-cache quantization ("Kitty") (#68945, WIP PR): --kv-cache-dtype kitty with a dedicated attention backend; values and most key channels at 2 bits, selected key channels dynamically boosted to 4 bits — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68945
  • Mamba2 NVFP4 via Marlin (#66675, PR): Marlin selected for ModelOpt NVFP4 Mamba2 projections on SM120/SM121 with Bolt-specific decode/prefill tuning — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66675
  • ViT full CUDA graph tracker (#38175): RFC for capturing the full ViT forward pass in CUDA graphs for Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5 — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38175
  • Rust frontend parity roadmap (#44280): the Rust frontend (VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1) is a drop-in Python API server alternative but still experimental — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44280

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B on MI355X/gfx950 (#57149): AMD's stacked-PR optimization plan for Quark MXFP4 — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57149
  • Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on MI355X/gfx950 (#59575): GatedDeltaNet (36 layers), QuerySparse Attention (12 layers), HyperConnection gated residual, MXFP4 MoE — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59575
  • Muse Spark 816B-A42B PTPC-FP8 on gfx942 (#64018): ROCm performance tracker — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64018
  • DP8 vs TP8 for single-KV-head MLA (#51454): on 8×B200 serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (304B/13B active, 1M ctx), DP8 delivers 7.7× KV capacity and 3.4× faster 1M-context TTFT at concurrency 8 vs TP8 — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51454
  • K/V cache view re-derivation in Triton/eager attention backends (#64572): views are recomputed on every attention call despite depending only on storage/shape/strides — same class as #59534 (FlashAttention) — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64572
  • Batch-invariant Qwen3-30B FP8 MoE tuning on Blackwell (#69184, PR): new Triton fused MoE config for TP=1, extending #63627 (BF16) and #66711 (FP8 on L4) — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69184
  • FA2 split-KV decode for sliding-window layers and spec-decode verify (#67649, PR) — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67649
  • KV offload re-queueing stall (#62532, RFC): 1.0–1.8s stalls for completed async KV pulls; proposal is front-of-queue re-admission — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62532

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SM120: extremely low decode throughput with --enforce-eager, CUDA graphs unusable (#56892, 8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, TP8). Highest-impact open bug; SM120 graph capture fix requested as priority — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56892
  2. ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120 dies or wedges under sustained load with CUDA graphs (#52540) — not the NVFP4 GEMM backend; 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52540
  3. Kimi-K3 CUDA graph capture silently corrupts output at batch=1 (#52531) — three distinct failure modes across cudagraph modes; silent correctness bug — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52531
  4. HF3FS KV connector reports failed loads as finished and never returns failed block IDs (#69058) — scheduler treats failed blocks as prefix-cache hits and generates over invalid GPU blocks — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/69058
  5. ROCm gfx942 engine hangs mid-step during CPU KV offload copies (#64549, GLM-5.3, v0.32.0, bare metal and SR-IOV) — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64549
  6. DGX Spark / GB10 engine startup collapses host memory (#56824) — NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY while MemAvailable reports ~22 GiB — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56824
  7. No working block size on v0.32.0 release tag (64 and 128 both fail) (#59203, CLOSED; fix tracked in #60762) — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59203
  8. DeepSeek V4 Flash upgrade failure 0.26.0 → 0.27.0 (#51758, stale) — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51758
  9. libcudart.so.13 ImportError (#52300, stale, CUDA 12.6 + vLLM 0.21.0) — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52300
  10. CUTLASS int8 w8a8 claims SM100+ support but dispatches nullptr (#54316, PR fixing #54311) — blocks Triton fallback — https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54316

Fix PRs in flight: #54316 (int8 CUTLASS gating), #63874 (FlashInfer one-sided workspace teardown), #62916 (KV connector engine-ID sync across PCP ranks), #69140 (Gemma3n sparsity quantile precompute), #69143 (Nemotron diffusion prompt logprobs).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • SM120/Blackwell workstation deployments are not yet production-safe for graph mode with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and ModelOpt NVFP4 models. If you're on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, validate output correctness at batch=1 and consider --enforce-eager only as a correctness fallback, not a throughput one.
  • KV connector failures can be silent. The HF3FS bug (#69058) means a failed remote KV load may be treated as a cache hit — if you run disaggregated prefill or KV offloading in production, add end-to-end output validation rather than trusting scheduler-side success signals.
  • DP8 outperforms TP8 for MLA models at long context (#51454): 3.4× faster 1M-token TTFT at c=8 on 8×B200. Worth benchmarking for your own 1M-context workloads before defaulting to TP.
  • Gateway integration is maturing: vllm.Render gRPC (chat/completions/Responses/Anthropic Messages, derender support) is being built specifically for gateway sidecars like llm-d (#65503, #67652) — relevant if you front vLLM with an LLM gateway and do tokenization/rendering outside the engine.
  • Quantization format churn ahead: the Marlin→Humming migration and the Kitty 2-bit KV-cache PR mean quantization config compatibility will shift. Pin your vLLM version and re-validate quantized deployments on upgrade rather than tracking main.
  • RL post-training frameworks carry monkey patches against vLLM (#68777 tracks these); if you integrate vLLM into RL pipelines, expect private-API dependencies to break across minor versions until the tracked patches land upstream.
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

SGLang Digest — 2026-11-22

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases in the last 24h, but the repo is active on the stability front: the SGLang 1.0 Release Tracker (#50045) is progressing as a "stability release" focused on hardening and explicit configuration errors. A notable correctness concern surfaced around --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 degrading long-reasoning accuracy on Qwen3.5-9B (#51531), and a PD-disaggregation bug where reusing a live bootstrap_room can return another request's output with HTTP 200 (#51980) — a serious multi-tenant correctness issue. On the performance side, AMD-focused Kimi-K3/K2.5 kernel fusion work continues via AITER/FlyDSL, and diffusion cold-start reduction is being proposed as an RFC.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

No new releases in the last 24h.

However, the SGLang 1.0 Release Tracker (#50045) is worth flagging: it describes a compatibility policy for the 1.x series and warns that upgrading from 0.5.x may require changes (upgrade notes included). The focus is replacing silent configuration changes with errors that name the offending setting — expect stricter config validation on the path to 1.0. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/50045

An in-progress refactor renames Kimi-K3 ROCm AITER and radix-4 top-k env vars to SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_* (PR #51240), with old names retained via aliases — no immediate breakage. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/51240

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • sm_120 (RTX 50-series consumer Blackwell): An open bug (#49209) reports that no model runs out-of-the-box with the CUDA 13 wheel install on sm_120 — relevant for anyone targeting consumer Blackwell. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/49209
  • DSPARK SM120 decode dispatch: A fix (PR #33407, closed) addresses non-instantiated topk width crashes on sm_120, with reproductions on 8× RTX 5090. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33407
  • Gemma 4 unified config: A fix (PR #34420, closed) loads official Gemma4UnifiedConfig classes instead of substituting the older Gemma4Config alias, correcting audio/vision section reconstruction. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34420
  • MiniMax-M3 on Ascend: A closed bug (#40735) notes incorrect routing of Ascend FuseEP through the normal MoE path. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/40735
  • AMD Kimi-K3/K2.5: Continued ROCm kernel work — KDA target verify via AITER fused FlyDSL (#48701), MLA value projection fused with MXFP4 output quantization (#33873), and MLA projection + RoPE + KV-cache write fusion (#32935).

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Diffusion cold start RFC (#51383, highest-priority): Proposes reducing cold start to ~20s for diffusion models (MiniMax-H3 from 80s → 20s), with the same PRs applicable to Wan 2.1 and LTX-2.5. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/51383
  • JIT kernel regression tracking (PR #52132): Nightly JIT kernel benchmark baselines with per-PR regression reports, following up on marker records from #51030. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/52132
  • AMD Kimi-K3 perf series (open PRs): Fused MLA value projection + MXFP4 quantization (#33873), Quark FP8 KDA in-proj/MLA absorb on FP8 kernels (#44362), AITER MoE sort from radix-4 router launch (#43126), and gfx950 KDA prefill extend on AITER Gluon chunk_kda (#47036).
  • MTP draft memory accounting fix (PR #35996, closed): Dedup of draft embed_tokens/lm_head previously ran after KV pool sizing, leaving ~2.5GB VRAM unused on a 27B-class model after startup. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35996
  • Custom all-reduce peer mapping (PR #52173, open): Maps each peer graph-input allocation once at registration to handle expandable segments crossing allocation boundaries. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/52173
  • Mamba2 _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel JIT stall (#51628): Compiles during serving on NemotronH (1.45s per compile, 2–3× per rank), stalling first large prefills — pre-compilation at engine init is the implied fix. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/51628

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. PD disaggregation cross-request output leak (#51980, OPEN): A decode request reusing a live bootstrap_room receives another request's output with HTTP 200 — a correctness and potential data-isolation issue in multi-tenant P/D deployments. Follow-up to #40125. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/51980
  2. Mamba SSM dtype accuracy regression (#51531, OPEN): --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 costs ~8 points on long-reasoning MATH-500 with Qwen3.5-9B (float16 unaffected); GSM8K-style checks miss it. Measured on v0.5.23, state-dtype handling unchanged on main as of cb97061. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/51531
  3. Hybrid-GDN speculative state memory blowup (#51175, OPEN): Speculative state reservation scales with draft length; a block-16 draft does not fit on 72 GB with a 27B hybrid-GDN target. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/51175
  4. Diffusion host-pin OOM (#51188, OPEN): MiniMax-H3 on 24 GB GPU + 32 GB host gets OOM-killed by host pin budget, yet the server still reports ready and returns 503. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/51188
  5. NPU silent truncation (#50443, OPEN): Qwen3.8-27B output truncated to 1 token when KV pool is smaller than input length (hybrid model, 128K on A2 32GB). https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/50443
  6. Prefill CUDA graph memory starvation (#40094, CLOSED): ~1.8 GB reserved by prefill CUDA graph competes with quantized-KV dequant workspace on small cards; server starts but stalls at long context while reporting 100% GPU utilization. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/40094
  7. HiRadixCache TP-deadlock (#28429, CLOSED): writing_check short-circuits before all_reduce when local ongoing_write_through is empty, causing divergent write_backup/load_back enqueue decisions. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28429
  8. fused_hc_head wrong result (#51106, CLOSED): Incorrect when hc_mult is not a power of 2 due to next_power_of_2 masking in the kernel. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/51106
  9. Triton fused-MoE illegal memory access (#40623, CLOSED): flashinfer_megamoe + EAGLE speculative decoding on GLM-5.2-NVFP4 sm_107 produced CUDA illegal memory access. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/40623
  10. DeepSeek-V4-Flash concurrency corruption (#33397, CLOSED): Progressive output corruption under concurrency on 2× H200 with dsv4 + DP attention. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33397

CI health: the tracking issue (#17050) reports 1 broken, 3 flaky, 981 recently fixed as of 2026-11-22 00:14 UTC. The CUDA Coredump Tracker (#26340) remains the highest-comment thread at 388 comments. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/17050

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Audit P/D disaggregation deployments for request isolation. #51980 means a recycled bootstrap_room can return another user's output with a 200. If you run disaggregated prefill/decode in multi-tenant settings, pin room allocation or hold off until a fix lands.
  • Don't blindly set --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16. The ~8-point MATH-500 drop on Qwen3.5-9B is invisible to GSM8K-style smoke tests. Validate accuracy on your own long-reasoning evals before adopting it.
  • Expect stricter config validation on the 1.0 path. Silent config changes are being converted to named errors; budget time for upgrade-related config fixes when moving from 0.5.x.
  • Diffusion cold start is improving. The ~20s cold-start RFC (MiniMax-H3, Wan 2.1, LTX-2.5) matters if you autoscale diffusion endpoints — shorter cold starts mean less pre-warming infrastructure.
  • Watch memory headroom on hybrid models. Speculative state reservation on hybrid-GDN targets (#51175) and prefill CUDA graph reservation (#40094) can both cause non-obvious OOMs or stalls on constrained GPUs; size KV pools and draft lengths conservatively.
  • sm_120 consumer Blackwell remains rough. The CUDA 13 wheel does not run models out-of-the-box on RTX 50-series; validate your target hardware before committing to it for production.
llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp

llama.cpp Digest — 2026-11-22

1. Today's Highlights

A dense release window (b12611–b12622) landed a large SYCL push (fused RMS_NORM, IQ4 reorder, gated_delta_net kernel), a model-level fix for .scale tensor handling, and new multimodal support for Kyutai Hibiki real-time duplex. Meanwhile, Inkling 2 / inkling2_loop dominated both issues and PRs: scale-pass ordering bugs, tensor-split support, DSpark speculative decoding, and Flash Attention bias work are all converging around this architecture. Multi-GPU and long-context behaviors remain the riskiest area, with active regressions on speculative decode and SYCL MoE prefill.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • b12622 — Model loader applies .scale tensors automatically (release). Removes internal _s overload of build_moe_ffn and build_lora_mm_id's w_s argument, moving precision handling to llama_prec_policy. Breaking for out-of-tree model code that called these internal APIs directly; downstream forks (e.g. unslothai/llama.cpp) will need to rebase.
  • b12611 — inkling2_loop shares loop slots after the scale pass (#32704). Fixes NVFP4 experts running without per-tensor scales, but reorders the load path; relevant to anyone consuming load_arch_tensors hooks.
  • No CLI or server config changes in this window.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Kyutai Hibiki real-time full-duplex via mtmd (b12619). Includes Metal fusion checks (5 RMS_NORM+MUL fusions verified in the new arch).
  • Inkling 2 / inkling2_loop ecosystem:
    • DSpark speculator support (#32218, open).
    • Tensor split (-sm tensor) — KV split, attn/ffn mirrored (#32751, open).
    • Compact bias on FLASH_ATTN_EXT across CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan (#32740, open) — without it, FA silently degrades to a non-FA route.
  • MiniCPM5 MoE GGUF inference support (#32644, open).
  • Nemotron 3.6 Academia — looped hybrid GDP + dense attention + MLP, with shared recurrent weights and per_loop conditioning (#32766, open).
  • Quantization formats: IQ4_NL / IQ4_XS weight reorder on SYCL (b12618); IQ3_S and IQ2_S AVX-512 vec_dot kernels (CPU, x86-64 only) (#32774, #32775).

4. Performance & Optimization

Landed (this release window):

  • SYCL (b12622–b12620, b12615):
    • Bounded CONV_TRANSPOSE_1D input iteration on Arc Pro B70 / oneAPI 2026.1 (b12621).
    • Column-blocked gated_delta_net kernel (b12617).
    • Fused ADD + RMS_NORM + MUL with vectorized RMS norm (b12615).
  • Vulkan (b12613–b12612):
    • Unrolled FA coopmat1 array to work around an AMD Windows driver bug (b12613).
    • Improved RDNA4 MMVQ rows for Q3_K, Q5_K, IQ4_XS on the AMD proprietary driver (b12612).
  • CPU: new memory access pattern in ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat_one_chunk (b12620).
  • AVX-512 iq3_s (-march=native, Xeon Platinum 8573C, n=2816): reported best-of-5 at ~? µs vs AVX2 fallback (numbers in PR) (#32774); iq2_s AVX-512 intrinsics also landed as a separate PR (#32775).
  • Inkling 2 DSpark measured (16 GB card, long context): after fixing q4 draft KV + graph-rebuild cost + adaptive pausing, a fixed 4-token draft runs 80 tok/s on code vs 47.6 tok/s without speculation (#32773).
  • Vulkan CONV_2D/3D shared-memory tiling with halo + split_k overhaul (#32629, open).

In flight:

  • CUDA/HIP/Vulkan Flash Attention bias for Inkling 2 (#32740).
  • HIP MMQ on non-WMMA archs (#32266).
  • Quantize target-size / target-bpw auto-tuning across mixed quant types (#15550).

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity (highest first):

# Severity Issue Status
1 Critical inkling2_loop: perplexity = NaN on CUDA — reproduced on b12600 and master; specifically called out as blocking Fix candidate in #32704; testers report it works on top of master
2 Critical Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid Gated DeltaNet): ~25× decode collapse beyond ~80K context — prompt processing fine, decode falls off a cliff. Linux/WSL2 + RTX 4080 SUPER Open, no fix PR
3 High CUDA ADD/GELU slower on B200 since PDL commit — first bad 7b28f950 Open
4 High Draft-MTP halves prompt processing on multi-GPU layer split (single GPU fine) — RTX 4090 ×2, CUDA 12.0 Open since August
5 High Inkling 2 IQ4_NL prefill abominably slow + crashes on RTX 5090 Open
6 High DFlash/MTP emits OOB token id == n_vocab (248320) on Vulkan gfx1150 Open
7 High SYCL: XMX-ESIMD path makes MoE prompt processing ~35% slower on Arc Pro B70 — regression in d81d0d8fb Open
8 Medium Q8_0 dot product sign error when int8 operand = -128 (non-VNNI mul_sum_i8_pairs_float) Closed/stale; unclear if fixed
9 Medium Flash attention garbage output at long context on gfx1201 (RDNA4), head_dim 256 Open
10 Medium Vulkan FLASH_ATTN_EXT wrong results on MoltenVK 1.4.2 + AMD RDNA1 — Intel Mac + AMD eGPU Closed/stale; verify on re-open
11 Medium DFlash spec fails with --split-mode tensor (shared output.weight in Meta buffer) Open
12 Medium HIP: CU_CHECK(err) in VMM pool lets cuMemAddressReserve spin forever Open
13 Medium Segfault after upgrading hip-runtime-amd to 10.1-2.1, RX 9070 XT Open
14 Low llama-server Web UI: effect_update_depth_exceeded at Chrome font-size ≥ 24 Open
15 Low llama-server (RPC client) occasionally ignores SIGTERM after long sessions Closed/stale
16 Low json-schema-to-grammar: enum/const discards sibling constraints Open — grammar-level correctness for structured output

Notable correctness-adjacent fixes landed: SYCL CONV_TRANSPOSE bound (b12621), Vulkan DIAG/TRI FP16 zero D_TYPE(0.0) (#32379), WebGPU/Vulkan nonzero clear writes 32-bit words not bytes (#32727).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Do not deploy inkling2_loop on CUDA yet. The NaN perplexity issue (#32710) is unresolved on master; if you must, pin to master + #32704 and rerun your KLD/eval suite before trusting outputs. The scale-pass reorder in b12622 changes numerics subtly.
  • Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + long context is not production-safe. The ~25× decode collapse past ~80K (#27623) means any agent workload with >80K-token histories on that family needs a hard context cap or a different backend.
  • Speculative decode remains split-dependent. -sm layer + draft-MTP halves prefill (#27428); -sm tensor + DFlash hits a shared-weight-buffer bug (#27833). Single-GPU is currently safe; multi-GPU needs testing per-model.
  • Speculative decode is worth revisiting for Inkling 2 DSpark on 16 GB cards: measured 80 tok/s vs 47.6 tok/s on code after the q4 draft-KV + graph-rebuild + adaptive-pause fixes (#32773) — a genuine ~1.7× decode win at long context.
  • RDNA4 + Vulkan users on Windows: keep FA coopmat1 unrolled (b12613) and pick Q3_K/Q5_K/IQ4_XS with default MMVQ rows (b12612) — the proprietary AMD driver needs both.
  • Server embedders: /embedding with --pooling none still lacks per-span mean pooling (#32587); plan accordingly if you rely on sub-token pooling groups.
  • Structured output / grammars: enum/const sibling-constraint handling is still wrong (#30750). If you depend on strict JSON Schema validation, keep a post-hoc validator in the path.
  • Server ops: SIGTERM-handling flakiness over long agent sessions (#29933) means orchestrators should use SIGKILL fallback with a grace timeout, especially with RPC backends.
  • Build hygiene: b12622 removes internal w_s/_s overloads — rebase any fork that patched build_moe_ffn or build_lora_mm_id.
Ollama — ollama/ollama

Ollama Digest — 2026-11-22

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases in the last 24 hours, but issue and PR activity is dominated by Inkling 2 (Thinking Machines Lab) support gaps — GGUF loading on Windows is blocked on a LLAMA_CPP_VERSION bump, while MLX users hit prefix-cache eviction and re-prefill costs past ~64k tokens. Separately, a cluster of long-running parser correctness PRs (thinking budgets, tool-call truncation, leaked close tags) continues to mature, and VRAM accounting/splitting fixes remain in review. Security/trust threads (Ollama Cloud ZDR vs. cached-input pricing, third-party inference exposure) also drew fresh comments.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None. No releases published in the last 24h. Note for planning: PR #17566 proposes changing the semantics of the think parameter (reasoning level vs. token budget split into separate settings) — a potential API-visible change if merged.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Inkling 2 Mini (26B) GGUF on Windows is blocked — unknown architecture inkling2_loop/inkling2 and projector inkling2v; ollama.com only ships MLX variants today. (#19817, closed)
  • Upstream llama.cpp now registers inkling2/inkling2_loop (merged Nov 21); Ollama's LLAMA_CPP_VERSION is still pinned at b12257 (Nov 10). A version-bump PR is the unblock path. (#19826)
  • Multi-file (split) GGUF import — long-standing request (#5245, 165 👍) now has an implementation PR: FROM model-00001-of-00002.gguf resolves sibling shards. (#19825)
  • Apple M4 Max MLX relative-attention kernels — reports same applegpu_g16s arch as M4 Pro but is missing from supportsRelativeAttentionPrefill / relativeAttentionSplitParts device lists. (#19820)
  • Jetson AGX Orin (JetPack 6) — request to build the runner with GGML_CUDA_NO_VMM=ON; vision requests crash in clip_encode VMM pool reservation. (#19815)

4. Performance & Optimization

  • MLX prefix cache fully evicted past ~64k tokens on Inkling 2 — relative-attention prefill peak grows with context, so every turn re-prefills the whole conversation. (#19819)
  • Inkling 2 prefix cache recomputes up to 2k tokens/turn — AlignPrefillToSnapshots forces restore offsets to match cold-prefill batch splits; routed low-precision experts batch-width dependent. (#19818)
  • VRAM accounting & GPU splitting fixes — addresses models incorrectly evicted, refusing to load, or unnecessarily spread across GPUs (issues #19463, #18679, #18349, #16599). (PR #19632)
  • Windows sysmem fallback — models exceeding physical VRAM spill ~13.9 GB into shared memory on RTX 3050 despite Prefer No Sysmem Fallback. (#19824, closed)
  • Split llama-server log lines — buffer incomplete log lines before parsing memory/layer accounting, to avoid misreported VRAM/offload values. (PR #19215)

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Vision requests crash on Jetson AGX Orin — CUDA OOM in cuMemAddressReserve (VMM pool) inside clip_encode; text-only works. (#19815)
  2. Windows /api/embed returns 400 — server-side POST to bundled llama-server on a high loopback port is refused (connectex) with embeddinggemma. (#19782)
  3. Qwen3.5 parser ends thinking early — a `` written as plain text tokens (not the special token) is parsed as a real close tag, truncating reasoning mid-sentence. (#19829)
  4. Tool-call/thinking parser defects (open PRs) — partial-tag check ordering lets tool calls open before thinking channel closes (#18624); unmatched thinking close tags leak into content (#18288); truncated tool calls handed to callers (#17564); missing closing brace recovery (#17565); reasoning budget cuts mid-word (#18212); assistant thinking not sent to chat template (#18281).
  5. Vulkan on Intel Iris Xe regression — qwen2.5:14b fails KV cache allocation on 0.33.3/0.34.2, works on 0.32.6. (#18531, closed)
  6. Silent CPU projector offload on OOM — llamaServerRunner.Load() retries via retryWithMMProjCPUOffload(), hiding unexpected placement; users want opt-in hard failure. (#19759)

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Agent/coding pipelines: parser fixes in flight are directly relevant if you run Qwen3/Qwen3.5, Gemma 4, or Qwen3-Coder locally — truncated tool calls, dropped closing tags, and premature thinking termination are partial-token-boundary bugs, not model quality issues. Pin a version and watch PRs #17914, #18288, #18624, #17564.
  • Long-context workloads on Apple Silicon (MLX): Inkling 2 past ~64k tokens currently re-prefills every turn; budget for latency/cost or keep contexts smaller until #19819/#19818 land.
  • Inkling 2 GGUF users on Windows: blocked pending a LLAMA_CPP_VERSION bump (#19826). MLX works; GGUF does not yet.
  • /v1 OpenAI-compat users: qwen3 thinking cannot be disabled via /no_think or reasoning_effort — plan around it or use the native API. (#17969, closed)
  • Embeddings on Windows: /api/embed may 400 on recent builds; have a fallback client path. (#19782)
  • CI/agents: a --no-animation / --no-animation-style flag is in flight to stop spinner frames polluting stderr logs. (#19828, PR #19830)
  • Security-conscious deployments: exposure hardening (TLS + API key auth) is still an open request (#14003), and questions remain about Ollama Cloud ZDR vs. third-party inference providers (#17489, #19823) — relevant if you route sensitive data through cloud endpoints.
LiteLLM — BerriAI/litellm

LiteLLM Digest — 2026-11-22

1. Today's Highlights

LiteLLM continues to ship on two tracks: a v1.112.0-dev.2 dev build and an LTS patch line (v1.108.15), with the project now emphasizing signed Docker images via cosign for supply-chain verification. The bulk of today's activity is a large redaction/privacy hardening stack (the #43697 split into 5 PRs) plus a wave of LTS backports for Bedrock, Azure AI, and Anthropic /v1/responses billing. Meanwhile, a broad set of provider-translation bugs — from Gemini thought images to OpenRouter reasoning chunks to watsonx streaming usage — remain open or freshly closed.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • v1.112.0-dev.2 — dev release; note the new cosign verify requirement for Docker image provenance. Release
  • v1.108.15 (LTS) — The ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:lts tag now tracks the latest LTS patch; downstream deployments pinned to lts will auto-upgrade. Release
  • Pending behavior change (not yet user-visible): PR stack #49377, #49378, #49379, #49380, #49381 will scrub prompt text from failure logs when message redaction is enabled. No runtime change yet — review if you have log-parsing tooling.
  • LTS backports landing (config-sensitive):
    • Azure audio transcriptions now honor the deployment's api_version from config.yaml: #53402.
    • azure_ai chat on the 1.108 LTS line fixes Foundry project / /openai/v1 routing: #53409.
    • Timeout semantics change for 42 providers using the shared httpx handler — split connect/read/write/pool timeouts are now preserved: #53391.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Gemini Live Avatar — Feature request closed for avatar_config / customized_avatar in realtime Gemini/Vertex integration, matching GA of Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar. #43166
  • Vertex Claude Haiku 5.5 structured output — Open bug: the Vertex model map lacks supports_native_structured_output, so response_format: json_schema silently falls back to an unforced JSON tool. #53478
  • OpenAI / Azure Skills API routing — Feature request closed to add native Skills API routing (skill CRUD, versioning, content retrieval) with Azure targeting. #37074
  • Ollama text-to-image — Request closed for litellm.image_generation(model="ollama/...") support (x/flux2-klein etc.), which currently returns empty ImageResponse.data. #28026

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Split httpx timeouts for 42 providers — PR #53391 fixes cases like Mistral ignoring connect=1 and waiting the full 10s read timeout. Direct latency win for provider calls under flaky connect conditions.
  • Overlong tool-call IDs in Responses↔Chat bridge — PR #53390 hashes >64-char tool-call IDs into deterministic 64-char IDs, preventing provider rejection and retry loops on replayed history.
  • Bedrock/SageMaker stream handling — PR #53482 returns 502 when a 200 AWS event stream decodes to no events (or ends mid-frame), enabling retries/fallbacks instead of silent empty responses.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Router re-executes auto-approved MCP tools on retry (High) — After a failed follow-up model call, retries re-run already-executed MCP tool calls. Closed; review if you rely on auto-approved MCP tool flows. #43153
  2. stream_chunk_builder TypeError on list-shaped reasoning_content (High) — Reasoning models (GPT-style) sending reasoning_content as structured blocks crash the builder at end-of-stream. Closed. #50893
  3. Amazon Nova streaming 100% failure (High) — httpx zstd decoder reuses a finished decompressobj on Nova's multi-frame SSE; non-streaming works. Closed. #35589
  4. Spend logs omit request/response payloads on v1.110.2 (Medium) — Regression: new spend-log rows lack content despite store_prompts_in_spend_logs enabled. Closed. #53263
  5. Responses→chat bridge double-logs cache hits ≥256 KiB (Medium) — Two SpendLogs rows and two logging callbacks on cache-served responses at v1.108.0. Closed. #52824
  6. watsonx streaming usage lost (Medium) — Proxy reports its own (undercounted) token estimate rather than the provider's, understating spend. Open. #46059
  7. OAuth client_id in query rejected on pass-through GET (Medium) — Broke browser OAuth for MCP servers on v1.110.1. Closed. #53185
  8. MCP tool discovery omits auth servers without upstream credential (Low/Medium) — Tools from auth_type: authorization servers disappear from /mcp-rest/tools/list on 1.108.11. Open. #52849
  9. Streaming drops OpenRouter reasoning_details-only chunks (Low/Medium) — Anthropic signature-only chunks and encrypted reasoning content are discarded. Open. #48401
  10. Componentized startup ignores YAML DB pool settings (Low/Medium) — Direct component entrypoints bypass pool limits/timeouts. Open. #33021

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Pin or float, knowingly. The lts tag is now a moving pointer. If you rely on reproducible deploys, pin to v1.108.15 rather than :lts, and add cosign verify to your CI if you consume the official images.
  • Mind tool-call retries with MCP. If you had auto-approval configured for MCP tools, audit your router retry policy — issue #43153 (now fixed) may have caused duplicate side effects in production.
  • Responses API users on Anthropic/Vertex/Bedrock: two complementary PRs (#53419, #53394) fix spend accounting for client-cancelled streaming responses; if you're on 1.108 LTS, backport #53419 for accurate cost attribution.
  • If you're building on reasoning models or OpenRouter: keep an eye on #50893 (fixed) and #48401 (open) — reasoning-content handling is the most fragile surface in streaming today.
  • Azure AI and Azure audio transcription users on LTS: plan for the routing/api_version fixes in #53402 and #53409; both are deployment-config-sensitive backports.
  • Privacy-sensitive deployments: the #43697 redaction stack is landing in pieces. No action required today, but validate that your log pipeline handles redacted-by-litellm placeholders once parts 2–5 merge.
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth Digest — 2026-11-22

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24h, but the merge queue is active: Inkling 2 (Mini and Small) LoRA/QLoRA training support (#18812) and AsyncGRPO tree packing for Qwen3.5/3.6/Qwen3-Next hybrids (#18817, stacked on the TRL cap lift #18809) are the highest-impact in-flight changes. Meanwhile, issue traffic is dominated by Strix Halo / ROCm memory-management regressions (#17605 closed, #18805 opened as a follow-up) and a cluster of Studio model-loading failures for Inkling-2-Mini GGUF and Qwen-Image-Edit.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

No new releases in the last 24h. However, several in-flight PRs carry behavioral/config implications worth tracking:

  • TRL cap lifted from <=1.15.0 to 1.18.2 — #18809. The old cap was never tied to a known break; AsyncGRPO tree packing requires TRL >= 1.17. Users pinning TRL should expect the resolver to move.
  • speculative_config now passed through to vLLM only — #18764, companion to unsloth-zoo#2640. Adds general speculative decoding config (EAGLE/EAGLE3, MTP, ngram, draft model, DFlash, suffix) budgeted inside the same LoRA lookahead/memory-fitting path.
  • UNSLOTH_MEMORY_REPORT=1 now reports host RAM on CPU backend — #18807. Previously a no-op on CPU; now prints process RSS, peak, and available RAM.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Inkling 2 (Mini and Small) LoRA/QLoRA training — #18812. Adds training for thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini (inkling2_loop) and Inkling-2-Small (inkling2), native in transformers 5.24.0. Requires companion unsloth-zoo#2657 for MoE experts and an eager attention residual. Note: Inference-side Inkling-2-Mini GGUF loading is currently broken in Studio — see Stability section.
  • AsyncGRPO tree packing for Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 / Qwen3-Next — #18817. TRL 1.17+ packs AsyncGRPO rows as a prefix trie and ships tree kernels for gated DeltaNet hybrid (recurrent) layers.
  • Gemma linear RoPE scaling fix — #18818. Since transformers 4.48, GemmaModel builds rotary embeddings differently; when max_seq_length exceeds Gemma's native 8192 without rope_scaling, the loader logged linear scaling but Gemma/Gemma 2 trained and decoded with unscaled RoPE. Fix applies the loader's scaling past the native window.

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Full fine-tune save: cast each output shard as written — #18795 (CLOSED). save_pretrained_merged(..., save_method="merged_16bit") previously built a complete cast copy of the state dict before save_pretrained ran when dtype changed — an fp32→bf16/fp16 master put the cast copy on GPU (~+6 GB). Now streamed per-shard.
  • GRPO video: one copy per prompt, not per generation — #18794 (CLOSED). With G=8, the GPU held 8 identical copies of every video across the whole generation batch; pixel_values_videos is now deduplicated. Direct VRAM win for video GRPO.
  • Opt-in GRPO rollout tail cut for colocated vLLM — #18803 (CLOSED). Implements sufficiency-gated termination (TailRoll, arXiv 2611.22206) to stop decoding stragglers at tiny batch sizes.
  • Krea 2: denoise on valid text rows only — #18813. Carried 512 padded text rows through every block beside 4096 image rows at 1024×1024; now operates on the valid rows.
  • HiDream MoE experts run only on routed tokens — #18793 (CLOSED). The traceable _moe_infer_dense replacement ran every expert on every token and masked; with 2-of-4 routing, roughly half of routed-expert GEMM work was wasted.
  • Studio multi-GPU split-render activation peak fix — #18784 (CLOSED). Split renders recorded no learned activation peak, causing later loads to refuse the split and fall back to one card with the second GPU idle.
  • int8 CUTLASS race cache keyed on race code — #18797 (CLOSED). Previously hashed whole GEMM files, re-racing every int8 weight shape on any Studio update touching those files (notable on L4).
  • DiT block swap headroom from free VRAM, not total — #18801 (CLOSED). 12% was taken of the card's total VRAM, over-reserving on large shared cards.
  • Auto fp8 base for DiT LoRA on sm89+ — #18770 (OPEN). base_precision="auto" never selected the existing frozen fp8 path; on sm89+ it chose int8 (or bf16 with block swap) at 1.15x–1.x slower.
  • FSDP2 empty_cache synchronization — #18777 (CLOSED). With expandable_segments:True, native FSDP2 empty_cache calls only synchronized the segment stream; fix adds a proper sync.
  • Frontend build CI timeout raised 40→55 min — #18816. Job now takes 33–40 min and was being cancelled despite passing.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Inkling-2-Mini GGUF fails to load on latest Unsloth Studio Docker — #18757 (OPEN, 6 comments). Blocks inference for a model whose training support is landing in #18812.
  2. v0.1.920-beta crashes on model load — #18563 (OPEN, 6 comments). Desktop + web UI affected.
  3. QLoRA on gfx1200 (RX 9060 XT, RDNA4) aborts with HIP error: an illegal memory access in three fused kernels — #18403 (OPEN). Plain PyTorch/PEFT has no SDPA kernel for this arch; ROCm-only, RDNA4-specific.
  4. Windows Strix Halo: host-shortfall check still forces mmap after carve-out fix — #18805 (OPEN). Follow-up to #17605 (now CLOSED via #17607); the fix handles --lazy-mode on-direct and initial Windows ROCm/Strix Halo binding, but the host-shortfall check still overrides explicit --load-mode none.
  5. Qwen-Image-Edit GGUF: every generation fails with device mismatch in _adaln_continuous_forward — #18759 (OPEN). Studio 2026.11.9; adaln_precompute moves modulation to host.
  6. AMD NPU (Lemonade/FastFlowLM 1.0.13) model listing fails — #18763 (OPEN). "Extra data: line 2025 column 1" — breaking change in FastFlowLM update.
  7. Cannot load fine-tuned Q5_K_M GGUF: "quantization type 36 ... this build does not have" — #18722 (OPEN). Studio v0.1.922-beta, bundled llama.cpp build 12588. Affects Qwen3.5-9B Q5_K_M exports.
  8. Decode CUDA graphs: RNG capture flag not cleared after failed capture — #18814 (OPEN, fix). On T4, Qwen3 (4B) GRPO crashes at first step with "Offset increment outside graph capture." Fix PR exists.
  9. Dual RX 6700 XT ROCm crash — #18622 (OPEN). Log attached.
  10. macOS malware-script block during update — #18699 (OPEN). "A script was blocked because it contains malware" during Unsloth update on Mac; 1 👍.
  11. Studio tests broken on main — #18815 (CLOSED, fix). (Python 3.13, diffusion) failing test_diffusion_family_data_freeze and test_every_decode_rewrap_site_restores_the_o... on all PRs based on main; refresh of the FastWan diffusion family freeze.

Closed today (fixes landed): #17605 (mmap forced despite --load-mode none), #18281 (localhost binding from GUI), #13094 (server stopped while embedding documents), #18690 (Inkling fails to load on 32 GB DDR5 laptop).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Inkling 2 is a moving target. Training support is landing (#18812) while inference-side GGUF loading is broken in Studio Docker (#18757) and on 32 GB DDR5 laptops (#18690). Don't ship Inkling-2-Mini in production paths until #18757 resolves.
  • Windows ROCm / Strix Halo users should hold off on Studio upgrades if relying on explicit --load-mode none — the host-shortfall check still forces mmap (#18805), causing the excessive RAM/SSD churn that #17605 reported. The carve-out fix (#17607) is partial.
  • RDNA4 (gfx1200) QLoRA is effectively blocked (#18403) — illegal memory access across three fused kernels, no SDPA kernel in stock PyTorch/PEFT for this arch. If you're on RX 9060 XT, use CUDA or RDNA3 for fine-tuning.
  • If you export fine-tunes to Q5_K_M, verify load before deploying — bundled llama.cpp build 12588 in Studio v0.1.922-beta rejects quant type 36 (#18722).
  • GRPO/video and full fine-tune memory pressure is dropping significantly via #18794 (8× video dedup), #18795 (shard-streamed save), and #18803 (tail cut). If you were hitting OOM on video GRPO or 16-bit merges, re-test on the next build.
  • Speculative decoding config is becoming first-class through vLLM (#18764 + zoo#2640) with memory budgeting inside the LoRA lookahead path — relevant if you're serving draft-model or EAGLE-based deployments behind a gateway.
  • Studio's frontend build CI is flaky-adjacent (#18816) — if you maintain forks, expect the timeout raise to land shortly; don't chase "cancelled" statuses on frontend jobs as failures.

AI Open Source Trends Report — 2026-11-22

1. Today's Highlights

The dominant theme today is the "Agent Skills" ecosystem explosion: four of the top trending repos (Claude-BugHunter, superpowers, stitch-skills, last30days-skill, app-store-compliance) are skill bundles or harnesses for coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Token efficiency and context compression are emerging as a first-class concern, with headroom and caveman both attacking the "too many tokens" problem. Local-first and lightweight LLMs continue to trend strongly (minimind, home-llm, LEANN), while RAG is bifurcating into "vectorless / reasoning-based" approaches (PageIndex, graphify) versus traditional vector DBs. Notably, vertical AI applications for finance, video creation, and job hunting are pulling in massive community interest alongside core infrastructure.

2. Top Projects by Category

StarTrail-org/LEANN Python 13,808 MLSys 2026 Best Paper—RAG on everything with 97% storage savings while running fully private on-device. Strong academic-to-practice bridge.

3. Trend Signal Analysis

The single most explosive category today is agent skills and harnesses—externally packaged capabilities (skills, slash commands, methodology) that extend coding agents. Claude-BugHunter's +1,803 stars and superpowers' +883 make clear that the community no longer just wants agent models; it wants curated competence packs. This is a shift from "build an agent" to "equip an agent," and Google's formal entry via stitch-skills suggests the Agent Skills standard is consolidating across vendors (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity).

A second signal is token and context economics. Headroom (60–95% token reduction on JSON) and Caveman ("why use many token when few token do trick") both treat context compression as a product, not an afterthought—strongly implying that real-world agent deployments are hitting cost/latency walls. Paired with claude-mem and mem0, memory management has matured from a hack into dedicated infrastructure.

Third, RAG is bifurcating. Vector databases remain dominant by stars, but "vectorless, reasoning-based" retrieval (PageIndex, graphify, LEANN) is emerging as a credible counter-movement emphasizing determinism, explainability, and storage savings—likely a reaction to vector-DB costs and opacity. Finally, local-first and small models (minimind, home-llm, LEANN) plus another vLLM-related learning project (tiny-llm) suggest continued interest in owning the full inference stack, consistent with recent releases of capable small models (Qwen, Gemma, gpt-oss) that make self-hosting genuinely viable.

4. Community Hot Spots

  • Agent Skills Standards — google-labs-code/stitch-skills, obra/superpowers, elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter: a de facto spec war is forming; building cross-agent-compatible skills early could pay off.
  • Token/Context Compression — headroomlabs-ai/headroom and JuliusBrussee/caveman: directly attacks the #1 cost driver in production agent deployments.
  • Vectorless / Reasoning-Based RAG — VectifyAI/PageIndex and Graphify-Labs/graphify: worth watching as a possible paradigm challenger to vector DBs.
  • Vertical Agent Applications — career-ops-hq/career-ops, TauricResearch/TradingAgents, zhouxiaoka/autoclip: proves the fastest path to adoption is a narrow, high-value workflow.
  • Small-Model Self-Hosting — jingyaogong/minimind, StarTrail-org/LEANN, acon96/home-llm: the local-first stack (train → retrieve → deploy) is increasingly viable end-to-end on consumer hardware.
