Pattern: Fix-oriented PRs (1997, 1681, 1730, 1975, 2019) have the shortest path to merge. Ambitious net-new skills (1771, 1703, 1245) face longer review cycles.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is no longer for new Skills, but for making existing Skills trustworthy — reliable evaluation, secure execution, and correct packaging — with namespace integrity (#492) and skill-creator correctness as the twin focal points.

Report generated from public GitHub metadata. Comment counts for PRs were unavailable (undefined) in the source data; PRs are ranked by recency of activity and discussion density inferred from update timestamps and linked issues.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-19

1. Today's Highlights

Claude Code v2.1.328 ships a significant release: an auto permission mode for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 across Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and the Claude apps gateway, plus "onFailure": "block" support for mcp_tool hooks. On the community side, a serious cross-user prompt leakage report (#111061) in VS Code 2.1.327 and a file-system destruction report (#107274, rm -rf removing 12+ months of git history) dominate attention. Desktop app issues continue to proliferate, with duplicated keystrokes, Remote Control silently disabling itself, and artifact-sharing regressions all active today.

2. Releases

v2.1.328 (last 24h):

  • Added auto mode for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and Claude apps gateway; interactive sessions without a permission mode now start in it.
  • Added "onFailure": "block" for mcp_tool hooks, matching existing behavior for command and HTTP hooks.

🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases

3. Hot Issues

  1. #75182 — Assistant text before AskUserQuestion never displayed — 11 comments, 14 👍. High-engagement TUI bug: reasoning text preceding a tool call in the same turn is silently dropped in the terminal CLI. Community validation is strong (highest 👍 today). 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/75182
  2. #111061 — Cross-user prompt leakage (VS Code 2.1.327) — Other users' Opus 4.7 requests appearing in a local chat window with Remote Control disabled. If confirmed, this is the most severe security-class issue in the digest. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/111061
  3. #107274 — rm -rf deleted 12+ months of git history — A data-loss report alleging the harness issued a destructive rm -rf on macOS. Low comment count but critical severity; likely to escalate. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/107274
  4. #107318 — Shared artifacts unreadable after desktop update — 10 comments. Cross-account artifact sharing (read/edit/republish) broke when artifact tools moved to the new connector. Related follow-ups (#109194, #110440) suggest a systemic auth/permission regression. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/107318
  5. #104422 — Desktop auto-update restarts mid-workday — 9 comments, 6 👍. Four forced restarts in a single day on Windows; clear demand for user-controlled update timing. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/104422
  6. #80708 — Hung ps child processes exhaust macOS process limit — 8 comments. Long-running core bug where orphaned child processes accumulate until the per-user limit is hit. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/80708
  7. #102874 — Routines API returns 403 for active projects — 7 comments, 7 👍. fire endpoint reports "this project is paused" for active Projects — clear API bug with good community corroboration. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/102874
  8. #89158 — Desktop keystroke duplication (macOS) — 7 comments. Key events (not characters) duplicate, so fix this becomes ffiixx tthhiiss; related duplicates #92622, #105349, #110547 indicate a persistent input-handling defect. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/89158
  9. #94454 — BSOD in bindflt.sys triggered by Cowork VM + Python MCP — 7 comments. Windows kernel crash correlated with Cowork VM Service startup; related #92779 filed as invalid but same signature. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/94454
  10. #106422 — --resume resurrects messages removed by session.compact hook — 5 comments. Hook contract violation: compaction semantics are not honored on resume for session files ≤ 5 MiB. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/106422

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24h:

  1. #86537 — Fix duplicated word in CHANGELOG.md — Documentation-only typo fix ("to to" in the CLAUDE_BASH_NO_LOGIN entry for v1.0.124). Open since 2026-08-13; no comments yet. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/86537

Note: With only one PR in the window, no further items can be listed. The PR pipeline is notably quiet relative to issue volume.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from open issues and enhancements:

  • Compaction model control — #96316 requests compactModel / CLAUDE_CODE_COMPACT_MODEL so cheap models can handle context compaction instead of expensive Opus/Fable-class sessions (3 👍).
  • User-controlled updates — #104422 asks for update scheduling and persistent notifications instead of forced mid-workday restarts.
  • Artifact export parity — #110985 requests exporting artifacts shared to you (HTML/MD/PDF) with the same options as owned artifacts.
  • GitHub integration breadth — #106713 requests linking orgs for outside collaborators with write access to enable cloud sessions.
  • Browser/threshold permission ergonomics — #107921 reports allowed-site prompts firing per-action; a recurring theme around permission granularity.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Desktop app instability dominates: keystroke duplication (#89158, #92622, #105349, #110547), auto-update restarts (#104422), and Remote Control silently disabling itself (#87777 closed, #111057 open) form a cluster of desktop reliability complaints.
  • Artifact sharing/auth regressions: a web of interrelated bugs (#107318, #109194, #110440, #110628, #110603) where cross-account and cross-org artifact access behaves inconsistently between claude.ai, Claude Code, and the desktop connector model.
  • Process and resource leaks: hung ps children (#80708) and Cowork VM-related BSODs (#94454) point to lifecycle management gaps on macOS and Windows.
  • Cost accounting trust: #97997 reports Fable weekly usage counted despite zero Fable requests, echoing prior #96035 — billing transparency remains a friction point.
  • Model reliability concerns: #105340 describes the model fabricating <task-notification>/Monitor events and then reporting results from them — a hallucination pattern with real workflow risk.

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-11-19

The Codex team shipped rust-v0.170.0, which introduces WebRTC negotiation for realtime voice calls in the TUI, auto-refreshed OpenTelemetry auth headers, and experimental cross-environment MCP server support. Meanwhile, the community's attention is dominated by a wave of Windows Computer Use regressions — two related issues (#57101, #56941) account for nearly 90 combined comments, describing persistent screen-capture overlays and system-wide UI lag that only clears when codex-computer-use.exe is killed. A steady stream of ecosystem integrations (MCP servers for mail, social posting, video editing) continues to arrive via Show and tell.

2. Releases

rust-v0.170.0 (stable)

  • New Features:
    • WebRTC negotiation for realtime voice calls in the TUI (#61172)
    • Automatically refreshed authentication headers for OpenTelemetry HTTP exporters (#61028)
    • Experimental support for identically named MCP servers across environments (#60905)
  • Bug Fixes: none listed in this release.

Pre-releases: rust-v0.172.0-alpha.1 and rust-v0.171.0-alpha.13 were published with no accompanying changelog notes — likely incremental alpha cadence ahead of the 0.171/0.172 stable cut.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #57101 — Windows Computer Use: capture access and gold display border persist after turn completes (64 comments, 👍12). The highest-traffic issue in the window. Users report that the yellow/gold screen-capture border and capture entitlement remain active after a screenshot-producing turn ends, raising both privacy and UX concerns. Community is clearly treating this as a blocker for Computer Use on Windows.

  2. #56941 — System-wide UI lag persists after Computer Use; killing codex-computer-use.exe fixes it (27 comments, 👍3). A companion symptom to #57101. The "kill the helper process to restore the machine" workaround has become the de facto mitigation and is fueling broader distrust of the Computer Use pipeline on Windows.

  3. #29922 — Feature: agent-callable monitor tool to wake Codex on background events (25 comments, 👍10). A well-argued proposal to escape the turn-driven model: let Codex subscribe to logs, files, builds, and CI events instead of polling. Strong support from agent-workflow developers.

  4. #21252 — CLI option to hide tool activity in TUI (24 comments, 👍47). Highest upvote count in the top set. Long-running sessions become unreadable when tool-call cells dominate the transcript; users want a toggle to view only reasoning and answers.

  5. #42950 — Public Codex "Sites" blocked by Cloudflare for external visitors (18 comments). A deployment/connectivity bug that breaks published sites for their intended audience — a sharp edge for anyone using Sites for real distribution.

  6. #51636 — macOS Work: Enter / send button silently fails to submit messages (18 comments). A regression that stalls Work conversations entirely, with no error surfaced. Reproduces across two projects and survives restarts.

  7. #24610 — Add explicit deletion controls for archived cloud sessions (17 comments, 👍32). High-signal privacy request: archiving is not deletion, and archived sessions may contain sensitive repo context. Data-retention concern for teams.

  8. #33782 — Desktop freeze on large image-heavy threads (ResizeObserver loop) (13 comments). A rendering-layer hang that traps users in specific threads; the ResizeObserver detail gives maintainers a concrete lead.

  9. #33593 — Shared models_cache.json oscillates between originator-specific catalogs across app-server processes (8 comments). Subtle multi-process cache coherence bug; relevant to anyone running app-server alongside CLI.

  10. #62394 — Adaptive Development Mode with task-aware multi-agent orchestration and model routing (2 comments, new). Fresh proposal to reduce manual model/mode switching across CLI, IDE, and App surfaces — the kind of orchestration feature the community has been circling for months.

4. Key PR Progress

Nearly all top PRs this window are attributed to copyberry[bot] — an automated projection pipeline landing a large, coordinated batch of TUI, sandbox, and app-server work.

  1. #62403 — Reconcile unfinished Cloud replies in the TUI transcript. Fixes stale prefixes left when a restored Cloud reply is marked complete before its final text arrives. Directly targets transcript correctness.

  2. #62390 — Highlight clickable links and controls on hover in the fullscreen TUI. Pointer-shape alone wasn't enough; hover now changes foreground color to make clickable regions visible.

  3. #62389 — Pause runtime sandbox integrity checks. Removes telemetry-only integrity checks that duplicate policy preparation, trimming launch-path overhead for command execution.

  4. #62386 — Prepare managed proxy settings once per sandbox command. Prevents launch-time re-preparation from overwriting credentials already bound to a command's shell environment.

  5. #62377 / #62376 / #62375 — Cross-platform path handling for workspace roots, sandbox writable roots, and thread working directories. A trio of fixes so a Unix client talking to a Windows app-server (and vice versa) no longer rejects C:\... paths as relative. Important for remote/SSH workflows.

  6. #62374 — Reconsider denials in attached Guardian reviews. Moves denial reconsideration into the shared verdict path so attached Guardian reviews behave like standalone reviews.

  7. #62373 — Opt-in in-memory message boards for Guardian v3. Each root thread gets an in-memory SQLite board shared by housekeeper and reviewer until the last handle closes.

  8. #62372 — Configurable Guardian V3 routing and retrieval guidance. Makes evidence-grouping instructions tunable and reduces context pressure from long routing prompts.

  9. #62366 — Enable lazy startup for stdio MCP servers by default. mcp_lazy_stdio_startup goes stable: with a cached tool catalog, optional stdio MCP servers defer process start until first tool call.

  10. #62370 — Share config layer entries across snapshots via Arc. Avoids deep-copying TOML data on every ConfigLayerStack clone — a quiet but meaningful config-path performance win.

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #16329 — Awesome Codex CLI: 150+ ecosystem tools (11 comments). A curated index of subagents, skills, plugins, and MCP servers, born from the pain of scattered discovery. Still the most-commented discussion in the set.
  • #60116 — Pushary: approve Codex actions from your phone (2 comments). Hosted service bridging Codex native hooks + MCP so policy-gated shell/patch/MCP calls surface on mobile. Also supports "send a git push to your team lead."
  • #62355 — Slidr: desktop presentation editor driven by Codex via a Deck API. Codex CLI runs against a Deck API to read/edit/render slides.
  • #62324 — Yaptake: Mac video editor controllable through transcript + Codex plugin.
  • #62259 — Postage: Mac mail client with a built-in MCP server for Codex (IMAP, localhost-only, revocable tokens).
  • #62244 — Octopost: remote MCP server to post to X, Bluesky, Mastodon, LinkedIn.
  • #62316 — Built with Codex: Last Plank and Harbor Signal, two browser puzzle games.
  • #61667 — Plainer handoff note exercise (no-account, reload-persistence check).

Ideas

  • #62213 — Built-in one-click prompt enhancement for ChatGPT and Codex. Requests a native "Optimize Prompt" control in the input box, citing WorkBuddy and Kilo as prior art.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Autonomy beyond the turn loop. The monitor tool proposal (#29922) plus the Adaptive Development Mode request (#62394) both point the same direction: users want Codex to react to background events and self-select models/agents rather than requiring a human to drive every turn.
  • Transcript/UI controllability. Hiding tool activity (#21252, 👍47), rebinding app shortcuts (#42957), and hover affordances (#62390) all ask for finer control over an increasingly dense TUI.
  • Data lifecycle & privacy. Explicit deletion of archived cloud sessions (#24610, 👍32) and env-var leakage across daemon sessions (#53547) reflect growing concern about what Codex retains and shares between contexts.
  • "Full Access" that actually means full access. #59249 and #60450 both push against sandbox/authorization layers that override explicit user settings.
  • Pre-authorized scheduled workflows. #42696 and #58589 ask for scoped, one-shot approval handoffs so automations and MFA flows can complete without a live human.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows Computer Use is the dominant reliability complaint. Persistent capture overlays, system-wide lag requiring process kills, screenshot timeouts, and missing click geometry (#57101, #56941, #58773) suggest the Windows capture/helper pipeline needs foundational work, not patching.
  • Authorization fatigue and inconsistent permission semantics. Users report repeated prompts on already-approved task steps (#54854) and settings being silently overridden by workspace-write sandboxing (#60450). The mental model of Full Access vs. Approve-for-me vs. per-workspace policy is not landing.
  • App/server and CLI divergence. Missing models in one surface but present in another (#49464, #62187), stale model caches (#33593), and rate-limit display regressions (#45052) all stem from surfaces evolving at different speeds.
  • Silent failures. Messages that won't submit on macOS Work (#51636), login state that fails without actionable error (#61123), and in-app browser backends that never attach while the agent quietly substitutes Playwright (#59417). Users repeatedly ask for visible failure modes.
  • Disk and resource hygiene. The macOS runtime installer leaving ~381 temp directories consuming ~472 GB (#61570) is an extreme case, but it fits a pattern of background processes and caches not being cleaned up between runs.
Gemini CLI — google-gemini/gemini-cli

Gemini CLI Community Digest — 2026-11-19

1. Today's Highlights

The project shipped v0.69.0 and cut v0.70.0-preview.0, with a notable fix preserving literal $ characters during template placeholder replacement and a new /stats heatmap subcommand for daily token usage. Meanwhile, the issue tracker is dominated by subagent reliability problems: a P1 bug reports that MAX_TURNS interruptions are misreported as GOAL success, and a generalist-agent hang continues to draw strong community upvotes. ACP (Agent Client Protocol) parity work is also accelerating, with a cluster of PRs from the same contributor bringing CLI behavior—truncation, parallel scheduling, session lifecycle—into line with the ACP path.

2. Releases

v0.69.0 (stable)

  • fix(core,cli): Preserve literal $ characters during template placeholder replacement (#30136)
  • feat(cli): Add /stats heatmap subcommand for daily token usage (#30222)

v0.70.0-preview.0 (preview)

  • Changelog entries for v0.69.0-preview.0 and v0.68.0 (#30224)
  • Automated version bump to 0.70.0-nightly.20261110.g1603e9b

The /stats heatmap addition is the headline user-facing feature; the $-escaping fix resolves a subtle but disruptive templating bug.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #22323 — Subagent MAX_TURNS reported as GOAL success (P1, 13 comments, 2 👍). The codebase_investigator subagent reports status: "success" / Termination Reason: "GOAL" even when it hit the max turn limit before doing any analysis. This is a correctness and trust issue: orchestration logic and users can't distinguish real completion from silent truncation. The high comment count reflects maintainer retesting activity.

  2. #21409 — Generalist agent hangs (P1, 8 comments, 8 👍). Whenever the CLI defers to the generalist agent, it hangs indefinitely—even for trivial tasks like folder creation. Instructing the model not to defer to subagents works around it. The 8 upvotes make this the most community-endorsed issue in the current queue.

  3. #19873 — Zero-dependency OS sandboxing & post-execution intent routing (P2, 9 comments). A design proposal to lean into Gemini 3's native bash affinity by chaining POSIX tools, while keeping execution safe. Signals a strategic direction: sandboxing as the enabler for more aggressive shell use.

  4. #21968 — Gemini under-uses skills and subagents (P2, 7 comments). Anecdotal but resonant: the model won't invoke custom skills (e.g., gradle, git) unless explicitly told to, even when contextually relevant. Directly undermines the value proposition of user-defined agents.

  5. #22745 — AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping (P2, 7 comments). Epic tracking whether AST-aware tooling can reduce misaligned reads and token noise. Related investigations: #22746 (codebase mapping via tilth/glyph) and #22747 (ast-grep for reads/search).

  6. #22267 — Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (P2, 5 comments). AgentRegistry reads and merges settings correctly, but the Browser Agent ignores them at runtime—e.g., maxTurns. A config-trust bug that affects any team relying on project-level policy.

  7. #21983 — Browser subagent fails on Wayland (P1, 4 comments, 1 👍). Linux/Wayland users get a spurious Termination Reason: GOAL with no useful output. Representative of a broader pattern: browser agent failures that surface as "success."

  8. #24246 — 400 error with >128 tools (P2, 3 comments). When tool count grows large (issue text cites >400 in reproduction, title says >128), the API rejects requests. As MCP adoption grows, tool-count pressure will only increase.

  9. #22672 — Agent should stop/discourage destructive behavior (P2, 3 comments, 1 👍). The model occasionally reaches for git reset or --force when safer alternatives exist, and doesn't appreciate the danger of DB modifications. A safety-culture issue filed by a maintainer.

  10. #23571 — Model creates tmp scripts in random spots (P2, 3 comments). When shell execution is restricted via exclusions, the model litters edit scripts across directories, creating cleanup overhead before commits. A quality-of-life issue with clear reproducibility.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #30363 — fix(core): avoid duplicating pending prompt in managed history. Fixes #30069; prevents re-appending the raw prompt when history hardening has already coalesced it into apiHistory. Includes first-turn and multi-pending regression coverage.

  2. #30362 — fix(acp): report stopped agent reasons. Fixes #30199; surfaces AgentExecutionStopped reasons to ACP clients instead of silently ending with an empty turn—the ACP analog of the "silent failure" issues above.

  3. #30236 — fix(acp): run parallelizable tool calls together. Brings CLI Scheduler semantics to ACP; previously a turn with four sleep 3 shell calls took ~12s instead of ~3s. Meaningful latency win for ACP integrators.

  4. #30234 — fix(acp): truncate large tool outputs like the CLI. One seq 1 60000 call cost 369k input tokens over ACP before this fix. Closes a serious cost/context regression on the ACP path.

  5. #30232 — feat(acp): support session/close. Currently returns -32601 Method not found, leaving every session holding config, chat, and MCP connections. Enables proper client-side resource release.

  6. #30230 — fix(core): keep synthetic binary ack so injected audio/video stays in its own turn. Resolves 400 "Requests ending with a model turn are not supported" when read_file is used on media under Code Assist.

  7. #30247 — fix(core): avoid blocking PowerShell parsing during shell checks. Synchronous PowerShell startup and AST parsing freezes the Thinking spinner on Windows; this moves parsing off the event loop. XL-sized change with clear UX impact.

  8. #30335 — fix(core): stop overriding core.sshCommand with empty string. Git executes the empty config value, causing error: cannot run : No such file or directory for any SSH operation. A sharp bug with a one-line root cause.

  9. #30246 — fix(core): quote IDE CLI path for cmd.exe in /ide install on Windows. VS Code's default install folders contain spaces, so /ide install fails out-of-the-box on many Windows setups. High-impact platform fix.

  10. #30241 — fix(core): keep injected binary data intact when truncating tool responses. Since #30180, read_file on audio/video >48 KB failed with "Base64 decoding failed" because truncation cut into __binary_injection__. Part of a coordinated media-handling fix set with #30230.

Note: no Discussions data was provided, so sections 5 and the discussion-derived portions of 6–7 are omitted or inferred from Issues/PRs only.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • AST-aware codebase tooling. A coordinated cluster (#22745, #22746, #22747) proposes AST-based reads, search, and mapping to reduce turns, token noise, and misaligned reads—with concrete tool recommendations (ast-grep, tilth, glyph).
  • Persistent, file-based task tracking. #18836 proposes replacing in-context WriteToDo with CRUD-based persistent tracking to combat context rot and session memory loss; #21000 experiments with native file tools for the task tracker.
  • Subagent observability. #22598 requests subagent trajectories via /chat share; #21763 requests subagent context in /bug reports.
  • Sandboxing as a capability enabler. #19873 frames OS-level sandboxing not just as security, but as the prerequisite for letting the model use its native bash affinity.
  • Agent self-awareness. #21432 asks the agent to accurately know its own CLI flags, hotkeys, and self-execution patterns.
  • Per-workspace policy. #18397 proposes workspace-scoped policy over global policy.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Silent failures masquerading as success. The most damaging pattern in the tracker: MAX_TURNS reported as GOAL (#22323), Wayland browser failures reported as GOAL (#21983), and ACP prompts ending with empty turns (#30134, #30362). Developers cannot trust termination reasons, which breaks orchestration and debugging.
  • Subagent hangs and under-invocation. The generalist agent hangs indefinitely (#21409) while custom skills and subagents are ignored unless explicitly requested (#21968)—the agent is simultaneously too eager and too reluctant to delegate.
  • Configuration that doesn't take effect. settings.json overrides ignored by the Browser Agent (#22267) and symlinked agent files not recognized (#20079) erode trust in project-level configuration.
  • Windows and Linux platform friction. cmd.exe path quoting in /ide install (#30246), PowerShell parsing blocking the event loop (#30247), and Wayland browser failures (#21983) form a recurring cross-platform tax.
  • Workspace hygiene. The model creates temporary edit scripts in arbitrary directories (#23571) and occasionally reaches for destructive git operations (#22672).
  • Scaling pressure from MCP. Tool-count limits producing 400 errors (#24246) and token-cost blowups from untruncated outputs (#30234) suggest the tool ecosystem is outgrowing current safeguards.

  • UI/layout flexibility — Restore legacy two-panel sidebar (#48882) and add session split view (#58245) dominate. Users want the layout to adapt to their workflow rather than the other way around.
  • Workflow-control granularity — Undo-message-only (#7963), credential sourcing for non-interactive admin tasks (#64773), and --no-auth serve (#43039) all point to a desire for finer control over what the agent may do, remember, and authenticate.
  • Internationalization and terminal ergonomics — TUI i18n (#37216) and keybinding handling under WSL (#63947) show the TUI is now a first-class surface needing parity with app/desktop.
  • Model/provider transparency — #64702 (enabling a model doesn't show required auth/cost) and #64762 (Mistral Large 4 invisible on mobile due to status: beta) reflect demand for clearer provider metadata handling.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • V2 platform regressions on Windows/macOS/Linux. Recurring: ACP hangs on Windows (#64686), desktop RangeError crashing tool calls on 2.3.2 (#64676), shell output-capture directory missing on macOS (#64752), ALSA flooding on Linux (#41763). Cross-platform stability is the dominant friction theme.
  • Free-tier rate limiting. #64754 describes escalating ~9–10 minute cooldowns after upstream rate limits — the backoff logic is punishing users for provider behavior.
  • Auth/credential handling. Credential leakage in tool I/O and logs plus auto-approved destructive gh api calls (#64745), and V2 serve's new mandatory auth (#43039), compound into a security-vs-usability tension.
  • Configuration reliability. #64765 ("continually unreliable harness c.f. opencode.json and whitespace") captures broad frustration with token burn, scope creep into external directories, ignored instruction files, and unapproved command execution — a theme echoed by #64695.
  • Agent instruction-following. The "Big Pickle rogue" report (#64695) and #64765 both describe agents ignoring explicit constraints; this is emerging as a behavioral-trust issue distinct from raw model quality.
  • Watcher reliability on non-mainstream platforms. FreeBSD kqueue misses new files (#58393) and Android/Termux PRoot inotify restarts (#64655) suggest the file-watching layer needs hardening beyond Linux/macOS defaults.

Digest generated from github.com/anomalyco/opencode activity for 2026-11-19. No releases or Discussion data were available in the source snapshot.

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-19

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but issue activity was intense: 36 issues were updated, with a burst of untriaged bug reports filed and closed on 2026-11-18/19. The dominant themes are context-window and prompt-cache mismatches across OpenAI/Anthropic/xAI providers, virtual-model compaction bugs, and a wave of TUI rendering and extension-API polish requests.

2. Releases

None in the last 24h.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #11021 — ChatGPT sign-in reports 272K for GPT-6.1 Sol despite 500K catalog (OPEN, 16 comments, 👍8) The most-commented issue of the day. Pi under-reports the context window for gpt-6.1-sol when authenticated via ChatGPT sign-in, giving users a smaller compaction budget than the server advertises. Highest community engagement signals this affects a broad set of ChatGPT-authenticated users.

  2. #9656 — Mouse wheel scrolls prompt history instead of transcript in fullscreen on Windows + Zellij (OPEN, 15 comments, 👍6) Long-running, still-unsolved platform bug affecting the Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi stack. Direct terminal and Linux/tmux work correctly, narrowing the fault to Zellij interaction on native Windows.

  3. #10642 — Embedded SDK long-lived session memory never drops (CLOSED, no-action, 7 comments) A server embedding many AgentSessions saw monotonically growing memory: SessionManager retains every entry in file… even after compaction, and resume loads the entire file. Closed without action, which may frustrate long-running-host developers.

  4. #12060 — openai-codex: zstd-compressed SSE requests get 400 Bad Request (OPEN, inprogress, prio:p0, 4 comments) A P0 in-progress issue: the same body passes uncompressed but fails when zstd-compressed since at least Nov 9. Directly blocks long SSE sessions on the Codex provider.

  5. #12273 — GPT-6.2 Sol reports far lower prompt-cache reuse than 6.1 (CLOSED, 4 comments) On turn 4 of an identical workload, 6.2 cached only 3,968/12,931 tokens vs 6.1's 12,800/12,931 — ~8.8k extra uncached input tokens per warm turn. A significant cost/latency regression for Codex users.

  6. #12035 — Threshold compaction fires far below the window for virtual models (OPEN, 3 comments) _checkCompaction doesn't skip the threshold check when the context window is unknown; virtual models resolve to undefined, causing premature compaction. Compounds with #12265 (compaction overrides ignored for routed models), indicating the virtual-model path needs a systematic fix.

  7. #12090 — durable: cancellation handlers should be able to wait on signals/deadlines (OPEN, 5 comments) Requests that parked tool cancellation be checkpointable and resumable across host restarts — a durability gap for pi-durable workloads involving remote job cancellation.

  8. #10583 — durable: calibrate compaction retention to reported context usage (OPEN, 4 comments) Compaction gets skipped when reported usage exceeds the threshold but character-based estimates fall below keepRecentTokens. The Han-character tokenization analogy in the report highlights that heuristic token counting is unreliable for CJK content.

  9. #11529 — Tool order depends on registration order, busting the prompt cache (OPEN, 5 comments) MCP reconnects, tool_search loads, and extension re-registrations reorder the tools Map, invalidating prompt caches mid-session. A subtle but costly correctness/efficiency issue for extension-heavy setups.

  10. #12293 — Anthropic server-tool usage doubles context reading; clamp loops with max_tokens 1 (CLOSED, 2 comments) Three behaviors combine to make the agent unable to function with Anthropic server tools (seen with the advisor tool): doubled context accounting, a bad clamp, and a loop. Filed against pi 1.0.0 / pi-ai 1.0.0.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11370 — feat(ai, coding-agent): add DeepInfra, Nebius, Ollama Cloud, Scaleway, SiliconFlow, StepFun providers (OPEN) Adds six hosted inference providers sourced from models.dev, chosen by contributor activity and issue-tracker demand. The largest feature PR in flight; stacked on #11369.

  2. #12278 — fix(coding-agent): refresh scoped models on interactive reload (OPEN) /reload now picks up enabledModels changes without restarting Pi, with startup --models still taking precedence. Fixes #12277.

  3. #12283 — fix(coding-agent): handle external SIGTSTP like Ctrl+Z (OPEN) kill -TSTP <pi-pid> previously suspended Pi without restoring the terminal; now routed through the same path as Ctrl+Z. Fixes #12272.

  4. #12280 — fix(coding-agent): tree navigation no longer re-adds prompts to history (OPEN) Both tree-navigation paths re-rendered with populateHistory: true, polluting Up-arrow history on every navigation. Fixes #12279.

  5. #10680 — fix: support npm 12 pack JSON output (CLOSED) npm 12 changed npm pack --json from an array to an object keyed by package name, breaking install checks, publish dry runs, and local releases. Fix accepts both npm 10/11 and 12 shapes.

  6. #12275 — fix(tui): stop repeated scrollback redraws from mutable tool rows (CLOSED) Prevents full-scrollback redraws when a long assistant response or tool result keeps updating after its top rows scroll above the viewport — a meaningful performance/jank fix.

  7. #12274 — fix(tui): avoid input cursor flicker during streaming (CLOSED) Eliminates cursor strobe during streaming/footer updates caused by visibility-sequence spam. Small but high-visibility quality-of-life fix.

  8. #12276 — docs: annotate Pi agent source code for learning (CLOSED) Closed by the author as accidentally opened against the main repo; intended for a personal learning fork. Notable only as a reminder that source-annotation interest exists in the community.

  9. #12283 (see above) and its sibling TUI fixes (#12274, #12275) show maintainer momentum on terminal rendering robustness.

  10. #12278 (see above) — grouped with #12283 and #12280, these three haoqixu/acmerfight PRs form a coherent "interactive CLI correctness" batch alongside the TUI render fixes.

5. Hot Discussions

Q&A / Community Process

  • #12284 — Would a clearly AI-labelled helper bot be OK in #ask-for-help? (General, 1 👍) An explicitly AI-labelled support agent ("Mira" from Teydra Lab, with a named human owner) asks permission to assist in the help channel, referencing CONTRIBUTING's AI-labelling guidance. Zero replies yet — worth watching as a precedent-setting policy question for agent participation in Pi's own community spaces.

(Only one discussion was updated in the window; no Ideas or Show-and-tell threads.)

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from the full issue set:

  • Extension API surface expansion — read-only access to status set via ctx.ui.setStatus() (#12298), prompt-origin metadata (#12291), assistant message transformers (#11450), retry-decision hooks (#11932), opt-out of OSC 7501 "blocked" reporting (#12292), and decoupled message-send vs. agent-loop-trigger (#12290). Extensions are pushing hard for finer-grained control and observability.
  • Provider breadth & compatibility — six new hosted providers in PR #11370, top-level instructions for OpenAI Responses providers (#8388), and vision-capability detection for llama.cpp (#12282).
  • Durability primitives — cancellable/parked tool handlers (#12090), truncation of individual conversations (Tx.truncateConversation, #12296), and compaction calibrated to reported usage (#10583).
  • Virtual-model correctness — skipping compaction thresholds when the window is unknown (#12035) and honoring compaction.modelOverrides for routed models (#12265).

7. Developer Pain Points

Recurring frustrations visible across the day's issues:

  • Context-window and cache accounting mismatches — #11021 (272K vs 500K), #12273 (6.2 cache regression), #12293 (Anthropic double-counting). Users cannot trust the reported budget, which directly affects cost and compaction behavior.
  • Virtual/routed model handling is systematically broken — #12035 and #12265 both stem from getPhysicalModel() returning undefined for virtual models, breaking compaction thresholds and per-model overrides.
  • Prompt-cache invalidation from non-deterministic inputs — tool registration order (#11529) and cache rewinds on missing stop reasons (#12301) show the cache is fragile to ordering and stream edge cases.
  • Long-running session resource leaks — #10642's closed-without-action memory growth, plus SQLite write amplification (#12285) and cross-conversation entry management (#12296), signal that embedded/durable deployments are outgrowing current session-management internals.
  • Error-handling robustness — xAI's "currently at capacity" phrasing wasn't matched by retry logic (#12289), a stale-cwd sandbox failure (#12300), a pid-reuse kill hazard in pi-env (#12299), and a misleading 402 surfaced as a "pi bug" (#12294). Small edge cases with outsized user impact.
  • TTY/terminal integration friction — Zellij-on-Windows wheel handling (#9656), extension-driven editor repaint (#12295), cursor flicker and scrollback redraws (#12274, #12275), and external SIGTSTP handling (#12283) collectively indicate the TUI layer is the most active area of user-visible papercuts.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-19

1. Today's Highlights

The 1.0 Preview agent-loop kernel continues its staged landing on main, with tracking issue #17045 driving "one surface at a time" migration while follow-up #17284 collects deferred work ahead of a 2026-11-21 freeze. Reliability work dominates the day: transcript JSONL corruption (#17747), interrupted-append record repair (#17771), and export byte-budget failures (#17741) are all under active repair. Meanwhile, the managed-agent subsystem is expanding quickly — MCP connection parking, PR-watch injection, and DingTalk card rendering all landed as PRs.

2. Releases

v0.28.0-nightly.20261118.d9ac287c9f was published in the last 24h. The nightly includes:

  • Test coverage for a real scheduled /loop fire in the full-stack managed-agent E2E suite (#17506)
  • A verify-pr fix (release notes truncated)

No stable release this cycle; changes are nightly-only.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failure: Managed Agent gate, no test identified. Open since 2026-10-19 with 464 comments — the longest-running CI bot thread in the repo, signaling persistent flakiness in the managed-agent gate.
  2. #11680 — E2E Tests: sandbox:docker shard failure, no test identified. Open 69 days with 83 comments; illustrates how per-commit CI failure tracking can accumulate long-lived unresolved threads.
  3. #17045 — Tracking: land the 1.0 Preview event-driven loop kernel on main, one surface at a time. This is the architectural centerpiece of the current cycle; 24 comments and active updates.
  4. #17747 — Transcript JSONL write corruption: a partial record glued to the next record breaks the parent chain (degraded_history). A P1 data-integrity bug in session storage, filed by wenshao.
  5. #17741 — main red on export byte budget since 980bb332a9 (429 bytes over), inheriting three red lanes into every PR. Classic "one small overflow blocks everyone" build-system incident.
  6. #17774 — Model frequently attempts XML tool calls instead of JSON. User-reported regression tied to recent Qwen Code updates; affects long-running sessions.
  7. #17757 — "Do not follow rules": agent ignores the ask-permission setting and makes changes without approval. High-concern safety/trust report from a user; status needs-info.
  8. #17727 — Managed-agent: after a 409 on first message submit, anti-replay always rejects "retry the same request" — no user recovery path. Notable UX/state-machine bug in managed sessions.
  9. #13471 — SDK Java CI: hosted process fault gates on MySQL 8.4 / Java 21, no test identified. Another long-lived (since 2026-10-05) unresolved CI thread.
  10. #17245 — Regular timeouts to llama.cpp server cause tasks to restart from scratch; user notes opencode holds contention without issues. Points at reconnect/retry gaps with local backends.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #17771 — fix(core): delimit JSONL records after interrupted appends. Directly addresses the corruption class in #17747 by ensuring complete records remain readable after a partial tail.
  2. #17711 — fix(core): seed side-records-only sessions and close artifact-summary residuals. Completes six deferred review residuals from #17518.
  3. #17777 — feat(core): mark quota-exhausted fallback models terminal for the session. Extends the model availability ledger so exhausted fallbacks aren't re-probed every turn.
  4. #17736 — fix(core): bound the joined async hook context block. Prevents verbose async hooks from appending megabytes into the model context.
  5. #17749 — feat(managed-agent): keep idle MCP connections across suspension. Phase 2 of the stateless Hosted Harness; MCP parking behind a server setting.
  6. #17665 — feat(managed-agent): add PR-watch bound-session private injection. Injects CI-red / conflict / head-move transitions into the Managed Session bound to a PR.
  7. #17748 — feat(managed-agent): render DingTalk managed replies as editable cards. First provider-native card rendering with in-place edits as segments arrive.
  8. #17780 — feat(cli): open effort picker from the OpenTUI footer. Makes the reasoning-effort tier a first-class, clickable control.
  9. #17720 — perf(serve): index bundled startup chunks. Speeds up packaged serve and ACP startup via synchronous resolution hooks.
  10. #17709 — feat(web-shell): add the daemon chat intent lifecycle core. Slice 2b of the unified chat surface, separating admission from outcome evidence.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in the source; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from Issues/PRs in this window:

  • Session management & history integrity — the strongest cluster: loop-kernel landing (#17045, #17284), transcript corruption repair (#17747), sidecars and pagination (#17738), artifact libraries (#17778).
  • Managed-agent maturity — MCP connection parking (#17749), PR-watch injection (#17665), DingTalk registration identity (#17769), card rendering (#17748).
  • Channel integrations — QQ outbound rich media stalled (#17167), voice attachment allowlist (#15334), mid-turn message injection (#15630).
  • Web Shell UX parity — worktree Codex parity (#17237), archived-conversation search/filter (#17772), quote-into-composer (#12682), artifacts panel (#17689).
  • Local/self-hosted model robustness — llama.cpp disconnect handling (#17245).
  • Theming/accessibility — custom-theme gaps (#17724) and native screen-reader presentation (#17500).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Chronic CI flakiness tracked as per-commit issues. #14724 (464 comments) and #11680 (83 comments) show that bot-filed "no test identified" issues accumulate indefinitely, creating noise and hiding real regressions. Export byte-budget overflow (#17741) compounds this by turning main red and blocking all PRs.
  • Session/transcript data integrity. JSONL corruption (#17747) and non-existent EOF line ranges in read_file (#17668) erode trust in session history — critical for long-running agent workflows.
  • Agent reliability and instruction-following. Users report the model ignoring permission settings (#17757) and emitting XML instead of JSON tool calls (#17774), both of which break the turn loop.
  • Managed-agent recovery dead-ends. Anti-replay rejecting identical retries after a 409 (#17727) leaves users with no recovery path — a state-machine gap rather than a simple bug.
  • Backend connection stability. Repeated llama.cpp timeouts forcing full task restarts (#17245), with users explicitly comparing unfavorably to opencode.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-19

Issues: 486 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-19 02:29 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-19

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw shows very high sustained activity: 486 issues and 500 PRs updated in the last 24h, with a healthy merge/close ratio (215 of 500 PRs merged or closed; 131 of 486 issues closed). One new release shipped — v2026.10.33, an extended-stable (LTS-equivalent) gateway-only release bundling critical security and reliability fixes. The issue mix skews toward stability and session-state defects: top-commented open items involve gateway stop failures on macOS, synchronous persistence blocking the event loop, and SQLite WAL/update finalization problems. Overall health is solid but the project is carrying a heavy maintenance load of P1/P0 session-state, message-loss, and crash-loop bugs across platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux/K8s), which suggests the extended-stable line is absorbing fixes faster than regressions are being closed.

2. Releases

v2026.10.33 — openclaw 2026.10.33 (gateway-only, extended-stable / LTS-equivalent)

  • Represents OpenClaw as of end of October 2026, plus:
    • Critical security updates
    • Reliability and performance fixes
    • New model support
  • Migration notes: No breaking changes explicitly documented in the provided release note. As a gateway-only extended-stable release, it is positioned for operators who need stability over feature velocity.
  • Caveat worth flagging for operators: Multiple surrounding issues (#197083, #200606, #201463, #201538) describe managed-update/Doctor failures on nearby versions (11.1→11.3, 11.3→11.5), including "state-migrated-no-rollback" partial finalization and candidate-Doctor migration conflicts. Users upgrading into stable branches should verify Doctor post-install completion and plugin migration state.

3. Project Progress

Today (PRs updated 2026-11-19): 215 PRs merged/closed, 285 still open.

Notable closed/merged work:

  • #201568 (CLOSED) — test fix accounting for new turnTainted: "unknown" hook field; restores plugin CI lane. link
  • #201567 (CLOSED) — align Goal authority proof with admitted-run policy (fixes 120s E2E timeout after #201377). link
  • #201463 (CLOSED) — Git checkout updates no longer fail before new release starts on schema change / busy DB. link
  • #201557 (CLOSED) — SQLite nested page reclamation no longer deadlocks against foreground writer. link
  • #201087 (CLOSED) — openclaw status gateway token conflict hint made readable. link
  • #186942 (CLOSED) — round-trip LiteLLM thought signatures on openai-completions routes. link
  • #196367 (CLOSED) — reject captionless message tables instead of silently dropping them. link

Open but advancing (ready for maintainer look):

  • #201569 — retryable early chat metadata reads during startup. link
  • #201566 — concurrent chat-history searches stay responsive. link
  • #201545 — package updates can start while Gateway writes to agent DB. link
  • #196659 — browser page-text reads no longer mix documents on mid-read navigation. link

The day's theme: update/upgrade robustness, SQLite concurrency, and UI reliability, with several long-running platform fixes converging.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment volume:

  1. #191944 — macOS gateway stop fails: "Process ancestry could not be fully inspected" (37 comments, P2, UX friction) openclaw gateway stop and stop --force both fail on Intel macOS, blocking managed handoff. → Need: reliable macOS service inspection/control; operators are stuck between "retry from independent terminal" and "use Gateway update action." link

  2. #119720 — Synchronous agent persistence blocks Gateway event loop at scale (28 comments, P1, diamond lobster, message-loss + crash-loop) Long-running P1 spanning August→November; partial repairs landed (#140231, #138984) but core blocking persists. → Need: async/off-loop persistence and transcript maintenance for large deployments. link

  3. #197083 — Post-install Doctor WAL verification leaves 11.3 update partially finalized (25 comments, P2) SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified; updater refuses rollback (state-migrated-no-rollback) and leaves external plugin state inconsistent. → Need: transactional, fully-verified update finalization. link

  4. #123792 — Assistant turns render twice with CLI backends (20 comments, P2, session-state) Duplicate persistence via live per-block view + concatenated aggregate; affects webchat and Android, not Telegram. → Need: single-source-of-truth turn rendering. link

  5. #182891 — Prompt cache never reused (cache read dropped N -> 0) (19 comments, P2) Envelope rewrites and runtimeContextCarrier changes invalidate cache every request. → Need: cache-stable prompt envelopes — directly tied to cost and latency for OpenAI-compatible providers. link

  6. #153426 — Curated memory roots silently excluded by provenance ratchet (18 comments, P0, security + session-state, release-blocker rated) MEMORY.md/USER.md permanently dropped from bootstrap injection after an ordinary web-search turn; no diagnostics, no recovery CLI. → Need: recoverable provenance state, operator tooling, and diagnostics for memory injection. link

PR-side hotspots: #159478 (selective group participation, XL, compatibility risk), #141004 (runtime skill-usage audit), #192350 (GitHub integration → plugin migration), #129388 (context-pressure-aware continuation, XL, multi-channel), #194376 (gateway admission for sessions_send wake starts, cross-channel).

5. Bugs & Stability

Critical / release-blocker class:

  • #153426 (P0) — Memory roots permanently excluded from bootstrap after benign agent behavior. Security- and session-state-flagged; needs product decision + security review. No fix PR.

  • #119720 (P1) — Event-loop blocking from synchronous persistence; message-loss and crash-loop impacts. Partial repairs only; no new fix PR.

  • #194451 (P1, CLOSED) — /think and other directives during an agent turn killed the turn with SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError; #192585 had only covered /status. Closed with linked PR — this is a genuine win.

  • #196199 (P1) — Regression since 2026.10.10: native Codex helper completions fail to resume parents, pausing goals and locking users out. Needs info; high user impact.

  • #152965 (P1) — Hot-reloading a non-channel plugin disposes channel plugins without reconnecting, cutting streams and dropping inbound messages.

  • #191476 (P1) — Matrix rooms stuck on "Plugin matrix consumer is closed" after image_generate races inbound message. A fix PR candidate exists: #201554.

  • #198218 (P1) — Doctor/update maintenance livelock on stopped Gateway (reproduced on 2026.10.6 and 11.3); update-run admission re-hashes unchanged state DB indefinitely.

  • #135712 / #157712 (P1) — CLI state reads leak ~162 MB read-only DB snapshots into cache; reported 23 GB in 25 min from scheduled scripts. A modern relative is #170496 (per-read snapshot copies on busy Gateway).

  • #200606 (P1) — 2026.11.5 candidate Doctor blocks update with plugin migration conflict and changed=[].

Notable closed-as-resolved today:

  • #192667 (CLOSED) — macOS Settings slowness and dark-theme input visibility both resolved after gateway update to 2026.11.5 (reporter confirmed).
  • #164279 (CLOSED) — self-learning background experience review 0% completion (50 consecutive failures since 2026-09-27).
  • #151962 (CLOSED) — phantom user messages from internal runtime strings not persisted to transcript_events.

Fix-PR availability snapshot: Several high-severity items now have open candidate PRs on the board — #201554 (Matrix consumer recovery), #201545 (update vs. live agent DB), #201463 (closed; Git checkout half-switch), #201538 (finish half-switched Git update). The WAL/update-finalization cluster (#197083, #200606, #198218) still lacks a merged fix.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #170562 — Doctor recovery for stranded requester settle wakes — targeted operator recovery without hand-editing the state DB. High likelihood of landing given the pattern of adjacent Doctor tooling work.
  • #179954 (P3) — Per-entry chunking paths for curated memory — lets list-style memory/ files index one entry per chunk. Plausible for a memory-core minor release.
  • #169428 (P3) — Usage footer expose auth profile (model.auth_label) — parity with /status; low-risk, likely fast-tracked.
  • #154524 — Accessibility: chat messages as headings for screen reader navigation — accessibility investment signal.
  • #155039 — Manual team-sidebar agent ordering — operator UX for multi-agent teams.
  • #183048 — CLI to inspect/settle unknown_after_send outbound entries — Slack delivery reconciliation tooling; fits the reliability theme of the current cycle.

Prediction: The next release window is most likely to emphasize (a) update/Doctor hardening, (b) SQLite/WAL concurrency and reclamation, (c) cache-stability work (#182891, #198373, #155868 cluster), and (d) memory provenance recovery (#153426). These areas dominate both issue volume and active PRs.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points expressed by real users:

  • Upgrade trust is eroding. Multiple independent reports (#197083, #200606, #201463 pre-fix, #201538) describe updates failing at Doctor/preflight or finalizing only partially, occasionally with rollback refused. One reporter even confirmed symptoms resolved by updating (#192667), highlighting how update quality directly gates user experience.
  • macOS operational gaps. #191944 (stop fails), #195192 (Safari 27.3 missing composer), #167696 (Voice Wake ignores session route), #185578-lineage memory growth — Mac users are hitting platform-specific friction repeatedly.
  • Cost/latency anxiety. Prompt-cache collapse (#182891, #198373) and Chinese quota-exhaustion failover (#177077) directly affect spend and reliability on third-party providers.
  • Silent data loss is the most feared class. Phantom messages (#151962), dropped inter-session messages (#144594), memory roots vanishing (#153426), and duplicate/misplaced replies (#179003) all draw strong engagement.
  • Satisfaction signals: Reporter-confirmed resolutions (#192667), closure of the /think mutation conflict (#194451), and the steady flow of "ready for maintainer look" PRs indicate contributors remain engaged and fixes do land — but the backlog of P1 session-state issues suggests users would benefit from a focused stabilization cycle.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-running or high-severity items needing maintainer attention:

Issue Age Severity Why it matters
#119720 ~3.5 months P1 Event-loop blocking at scale; only partial fixes
#153426 ~2 months P0 Permanent silent memory-root exclusion; needs product + security decision
#112638 ~4 months P2 session.maintenance enforce silently unbounded; thread/channel entries exempt
#127195 ~3 months P2 16 call sites emit identical error with no reason code — undebuggable in production
#152965 ~2 months P1 Plugin hot-reload disposes channel plugins; drops inbound messages
#162585 ~7 weeks P2 Windows plugin staging never converges (290 MB → 612 MB); gateway never healthy

Backlog PRs needing direction: #159478 (group participation, stalled "waiting on author"), #129388 (continuation, XL, clawsweeper-recovery-stuck), #194376 (gateway sessions_send admission, very broad surface), #192350 (GitHub plugin migration, depends on #192349).

Overall health verdict: The project is actively maintained and responsive — 215 PRs closed and 131 issues resolved in 24h — but is in a stabilization-required phase: severity-weighted backlog is dominated by session-state, update-pipeline, and platform-specific stability defects. The extended-stable release cadence is a sensible mitigation; the main risk is that regression inflow (regressions like #196199, #198373) may outpace the fix pipeline without a dedicated hardening milestone.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report

Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem Snapshot date: 2026-11-19

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant open-source landscape in late 2026 is bifurcated between mature, stabilization-phase platforms (OpenClaw) and fast-iterating challengers executing architectural pivots (QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, Hermes Agent). Activity is dominated by the same core concerns across every project: session-state integrity, prompt-cache economics, update/upgrade trust, and security of persisted credentials. None of the projects is feature-starved — the binding constraint is reliability debt accumulated from aggressive feature velocity, with severity-weighted backlogs concentrated in P0/P1 session-state and update-pipeline defects. The ecosystem is converging on a common architecture (plugin-based extensibility, MCP integration, multi-channel gateways, LTS-style release lines), while differentiation shifts to target user, channel coverage, and governance posture.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Scale and maturity. 486 issues / 500 PRs in 24h is an order of magnitude above any peer. It has the only LTS-equivalent release line (extended-stable), a signal that operators treat it as production infrastructure rather than a project to tinker with.
  • Channel breadth. Session-state bugs span webchat, Android, Telegram, Matrix, Slack — evidence of the widest surface area in the ecosystem.
  • Ecosystem gravity. Community hot topics (#159478 group participation, #192350 GitHub plugin migration) show third-party extension pressure that peers have not yet attracted at comparable volume.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw runs a gateway-centric architecture with SQLite-backed transcript/session persistence and a Doctor diagnostic/migration subsystem. This is a heavier, operator-oriented design than peers.
  • Hermes Agent emphasizes CLI-first ergonomics with a Desktop companion; QwenPaw is mid-pivot to a plugin-extracted "lighter core"; ZeroClaw is SOP- and permission-tier-centric (fail-closed decision gates, multi-agent scoping).

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Four requirements recur independently across multiple projects, indicating ecosystem-level gaps rather than project-specific bugs:

A. Session-state integrity / message duplication

  • OpenClaw: #123792 (assistant turns render twice, CLI backends); #151962 (phantom user messages)
  • Hermes: #137287 (Desktop transcript duplicates/scatters/drops); #131591 (double-rendered turns); #156739 (internal summaries shown as user bubbles)
  • QwenPaw: #8806 (phantom user messages drive looping)
  • Shared need: single-source-of-truth turn rendering with deduplication across live-stream and hydrated views. This is the single most cross-cutting defect class in the ecosystem.

B. Prompt-cache economics and cost control

  • OpenClaw: #182891 (cache read dropped N → 0); #198373 cluster
  • Hermes: #156455 (merged — cache kept warm while it pays, then compacts); #157583 (cache miss after image turn)
  • ZeroClaw: #11696 (system prompt rebuilt from disk every turn busts cache)
  • Shared need: cache-stable prompt envelopes and idle-cache economics. Every project with multi-provider support is bleeding cost here.

C. Update/upgrade trust and transactional finalization

  • OpenClaw: #197083, #200606, #198218, #201463 — Doctor/WAL finalization failures, refused rollbacks
  • QwenPaw: #8811, #8812 — regressions introduced by v2.3.0.post1
  • ZeroClaw: SHA256SUMS verification parity for Windows installers (#12122)
  • Shared need: transactional, verifiable update pipelines with rollback. This is the top trust-eroding class — users explicitly state they are wary of updating.

D. Runaway-loop / safety-gate reliability

  • QwenPaw: #8712 (DoomLoopGate never fires in production)
  • OpenClaw: #119720 (event-loop blocking → crash-loop), #153426 (P0 memory-root exclusion)
  • ZeroClaw: #11124 (S0 SOP decision-gate bypass — now fixed by #12237)
  • Shared need: safety mechanisms that are proven to fire under adversarial/repetitive input, not just present in code.

E. Credential/secret handling on disk

  • Hermes: #62336 (terminal env snapshots persist credentials to disk); #157615 (redaction misses label-prefixed dumps)
  • OpenClaw: #153426 (P0, security-flagged memory provenance)
  • QwenPaw: #7757, #8028 (destructive-command and COM-automation guards)
  • Shared need: defense-in-depth for persisted state, with redaction classifiers that handle real-world secret formats.

7. Trend Signals

For AI agent developers, five industry trends emerge from the aggregated community feedback:

1. Reliability is the new feature war. Every project's top-engagement items are correctness defects, not capability gaps. Users no longer ask "can it do X?" — they ask "will it silently break X?" Silent failures (#9770 cron dropouts, #9896 memory-status lies, #151962 phantom messages) generate the strongest emotional response. Implication: ship observability and loud failure modes before new tools.

2. Cost/latency anxiety is now a first-class UX concern. Prompt-cache invalidation (#182891, #157583, #11696) is tracked as a bug, not a tuning detail. Multi-hour sessions are the norm, and cache misses translate directly to dollars and broken chats. Implication: cache-stable prompt envelopes are a competitive differentiator, not an optimization.

3. Update trust is a gate on adoption. Users explicitly report wariness of updating (QwenPaw "升级后出现"; OpenClaw's rollback-refusal cluster). Transactional finalization with verified rollback is becoming table stakes. Implication: invest in update pipelines as a product surface, not infrastructure plumbing.

4. Plugin ecosystems are the extensibility battleground. QwenPaw's "lighter core" pivot, OpenClaw's GitHub-integration-to-plugin migration, and Hermes' plugin-catalog PRs all point the same direction: extract capabilities into a governed plugin SDK. Theme-token depth (#8071, 21 comments) shows plugin developers will demand real API surface, not single-knob toggles. Implication: design plugin lifecycle and theming early — retrofitting is expensive.

5. Safety mechanisms must be adversarially verified. QwenPaw's DoomLoopGate "never fired in production" (#8712) and ZeroClaw's SOP decision-gate bypass (#11124, S0) reveal that safety code shipped without proof-of-firing is a liability. Implication: safety gates need test harnesses that prove interruption under realistic repetitive/adversarial input, not just unit coverage.

6. Provider-catalogue churn is a regression source. ZeroClaw's OpenCode Go bugs (#12412, #12413) and QwenPaw's gateway failures (#8718) both trace to recent provider-catalogue refactors. As multi-provider support expands, the provider registry is becoming a critical, regression-prone subsystem. Implication: treat provider registries as versioned, testable contracts.

Bottom Line for Decision-Makers

  • Choosing a platform for production: OpenClaw is the only project with an LTS-equivalent line and enterprise-operator tooling — but budget for a stabilization cycle and audit the P0/P1 backlog (notably #153426, #119720) before committing.
  • Choosing for extensibility: QwenPaw's plugin SDK is the most ambitious bet, but its post-release regression rate warrants pinning to tested versions.
  • Choosing for security posture: ZeroClaw's fail-closed SOP model and security-heavy close-out cadence are the strongest in the set — contingent on clearing its review bottleneck.
  • Cross-cutting investment: session-state deduplication, cache-stable envelopes, and transactional updates are ecosystem-wide gaps. A project that solves these cleanly will differentiate on trust, which is emerging as the scarcest currency in the category.

  1. Post-release regressions are eroding trust. Two users reported issues immediately after upgrading to v2.3.0.post1 (#8811 narrow-screen clipping, #8812 startup WARNING spam + channel unavailability). The phrase "升级后出现" (appeared after upgrade) signals users are wary of updating.

  2. Resource management under load is fragile. #8805 documents 1.78 GB pinned in glibc arenas on a 56-core host. #8802 shows context overflow aborting long MCP sequences. Enterprise users running multi-core Docker deployments are most affected.

  3. Runaway loops persist. #8712 reveals the doom-loop gate has never fired in production — a fundamental safety mechanism is silently broken. Combined with #8806 (phantom messages causing loops), users report agents executing indefinitely.

  4. Plugin API surface is too narrow. Plugin developers (#8071) want deeper theme control. The single colorPrimary option is insufficient for real plugin UI needs.

  5. Model gateway errors are opaque. #8798 — user hit MODEL_QUOTA_EXCEEDED with a confusing signup message; frustration evident in tone ("keep getting a damn..."). Better error surfacing needed.

Satisfaction Signals

  • Fast triage on #8806 and #7197 (same-day closure).
  • Official roadmap communication (#8808) from maintainer @Luohh5 is well-received.
  • The plugin ecosystem direction has broad buy-in from contributors (multiple XXXL PRs from different authors).

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention:

Item Age Why It Matters
#8071 — Plugin theme extension point 49 days open, 21 comments Highest-engagement open issue. PR #8787 partially addresses it but the issue remains open — needs a maintainer decision on scope/acceptance.
#8431 — Local Whisper SDK plugin 24 days open, no comments visible XXXL PR with no apparent reviewer activity. Risk of bit-rot as the SDK evolves.
#8469 — MCP plugin extraction 22 days open Critical path for the roadmap; needs review bandwidth.
#8499 — Local model management plugin 21 days open Same concern as above.
#8268 — TaskTracker run-completion cleanup 34 days open Fixes half of #8173; a hung callback leaves runs stuck running forever. Low-risk fix that's been waiting too long.
#8295 — Hide internal scaffolding at display boundary 33 days open, Under Review XL fix for leaking <system-info> tags to end users. Marked "Under Review" but stalled.
#8133 — Fix CJK emphasis boundaries in Markdown 42 days open, Under Review Affects a large user base (Chinese-language users); **中文。** never renders correctly. Long review cycle for a size/L PR.

Recommendation: The maintainer team appears bottlenecked on reviewing XXXL PRs. Consider designating additional reviewers or splitting the large plugin-extraction PRs into mergeable slices to unblock the roadmap.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-19

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw is in a high-velocity maintenance and hardening phase, with 50 issues and 50 PRs touched in the last 24 hours and no new releases cut. Activity is dominated by the canonical provider registry work stream (a cluster of stacked XL PRs from NiuBlibing, #12448–#12457) and a steady stream of security/robustness bug fixes. The issue backlog skews heavily toward S2 "degraded behavior" bugs rather than S0/S1 incidents, though one S1 (tool-context collapse on Claude Opus 5.5, #12401) is in progress. Notably, 10 issues were closed today across security, SOP, and observability domains, indicating effective maintainer throughput. Overall project health looks strong on triage responsiveness, but the volume of long-lived status:in-progress S2 issues suggests a growing stabilization debt heading into v0.9.1.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. The most recent release in flight is v0.9.1, referenced in tags on #12401 and PR #12237. No migration or breaking-change notes to publish today.

3. Project Progress

Only 2 PRs were merged/closed today against 48 still open — a low merge day, consistent with a large stack of dependency-chained PRs awaiting review.

Closed:

  • PR #12237 — fix(sop): use the fail-closed mode when the decision answers are unusable. Resolves the S0 decision-gate bypass tracked in #11124, where a malformed/missing gate answer could let an SOP start in Auto mode. This is a meaningful security hardening for the SOP subsystem.

Closed issues advancing features/fixes:

  • #12122 — Windows prebuilt installers now expected to perform SHA256SUMS verification (parity with install.sh).
  • #12146 — MCP SSE client no longer accepts an absolute endpoint URL and leaks bearer tokens cross-origin.
  • #12144 — file_upload/file_edit no longer authorize through the write tier, closing a sibling-workspace read escalation.
  • #12053 — Unpinned third-party script on /api/docs origin addressed.
  • #12280 — Forwarded loopback addresses no longer treated as local for SOP cancel authorization.
  • #10318 — Concurrent SOP authoring writes serialized.
  • #9655, #9736, #12169 — Telegram approval-card positioning, SessionState persistence gap, and send_message_to_peer tool-scope leakage respectively.

Net: a security-heavy close-out day, especially around SOP authorization, multi-agent permission tiers, and channel-secret handling.

4. Community Hot Topics

Rank Item Comments Underlying need
1 #12401 — keep_tool_context_turns breaks Claude Opus 5.5 chats with thinking-signature 400 6 Users need long-running tool-use sessions to survive context windowing without poisoning the conversation permanently.
2 #9770 — cron update silently discards declarative job changes (six columns) 3 Silent data loss in declarative config is eroding trust in zeroclaw cron as a source-of-truth workflow.
3 #9655 (closed) — Approval cards carry no position 3 Multi-tool-call turns in Telegram are unreviewable when cards are indistinguishable — an operator UX blocker.
4 #9736 (closed) — RPC prompt path never writes persisted SessionState 3 RPC-attached surfaces (zerocode, gateway) need state parity with the WebSocket path.
5 #11696 — System prompt rebuilt from disk every turn busts prompt cache 3 Cost regression for operators running many live sessions; personality-file edits invalidate everyone.

The theme across hot topics is operational trust: users are hitting edge cases where the agent silently misbehaves (400-loop, silent config drops, cache invalidation) rather than erroring loudly.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

S1 — Workflow blocked

  • #12401 — Claude Opus 5.5 chats permanently fail after older tool turns leave keep_tool_context_turns. status:in-progress, tagged release:v0.9.1. No fix PR linked yet — this is the highest-priority stability item today.

S0 — Security/data risk (now closed)

  • #11124 — SOP decision gate strict fallback bypass. Fixed by PR #12237.

S2 — Degraded behavior (open, new/updated today)

  • #12504 — Anthropic provider replays unsigned thinking block; every retry fails with signature: Field required. Related to #12401.
  • #12558 — Matrix tool-approval prompts posted to room timeline instead of thread.
  • #12559 — Config setters accept inf/NaN/1e999 for decimal settings.
  • #12413 & #12412 — OpenCode Go context-window discovery returns no capacity; OpenCode Go uses Zen's catalogue. Both v0.9.0 regressions.
  • #11823 — Shell scanner skips command substitution in unquoted-delimiter heredoc bodies (sandbox bypass).
  • #9896 — Status banner reports Memory: none when backend is sqlite.
  • #11696 — Per-turn prompt rebuild cost regression.

Pattern note: Two Anthropic thinking-signature bugs (#12401, #12504) filed within a week suggest the new Claude Opus 5.5 thinking-block handling needs a consolidated fix.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

New/enhancement requests today:

  • #12562 — Telegram trusted_groups: allow group-member messages without per-sender allowlist entries. Likely candidate for a channel-focused minor release — small surface, clear operator value.
  • #12561 — Matrix: bounded cleanup of declined room invites (follow-up to #12495).
  • #11050 — Pace native polls with other outbound channel messages (WhatsApp).
  • #9914 — Preserve Docker coding CLI workspace root with relative cwd.
  • #9685 — sops/cancel RPC method (explicitly deferred until #9476 merges).
  • #11768 — Honor HTTP Retry-After for provider 429s.

Prediction: Expect messaging-channel polish (Telegram trusted groups, Matrix invite cleanup, WhatsApp poll pacing) to land in v0.9.2, while the SOP cancel RPC (#9685) waits on the SOP MVP cutover. The canonical provider registry stack (#12448–#12457) is clearly the flagship feature for the v0.10 line, not v0.9.x.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points surfaced today:

  • Cost & cache sensitivity — #11696 and #12401 both stem from how prompt/tool context is assembled per turn. Multi-hour sessions are the norm, and users are feeling the cost in both dollars and broken chats.
  • Silent failures over loud ones — #9770 (cron update dropout) and #9896 (memory status lie) both describe the system telling the user things worked when they didn't. This is the most consistent friction theme.
  • Channel operator UX — #9655 (approval cards) and #12558 (Matrix thread vs. timeline) show approval flows still assume a single-tool-call, non-threaded world.
  • Provider ecosystem churn — Two OpenCode Go bugs (#12412, #12413) in the same 24h window indicate the v0.9.0 provider-catalogue refactor introduced model-list regressions.

Satisfaction signals: The rapid closure of 10 issues (many security-tagged) suggests users are filing well-scoped reports and maintainers are landing fixes — a healthy loop. No 👍 reactions on any tracked item, so sentiment data is comment-volume only.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived or high-risk items deserving maintainer attention:

  • #9492 (open since 2026-07-28, p1, risk:high) — auth refresh dead-ends when an external client rotated the shared OpenAI-Codex refresh token. Nearly 4 months old with only 1 comment; single-use rotating tokens make this a recurring footgun.
  • #9770 (open since 2026-08-05, p1) — Cron update silently discards declarative changes. High-trust-impact silent data loss still unfixed after 3.5 months.
  • #10391 (open since 2026-08-26, size:XL, risk:high, needs-author-action) — The delegate workspace/tool-ceiling bounding fix. Three master merges into the branch and still not landed; blocks #9872.
  • #10412 (open since 2026-08-27, size:XL, breaking-change, p1) — Shared SessionBackend atomic ownership contract. Foundational for RPC/WebSocket admission parity but stalled.
  • #11847 (open since 2026-10-19, size:XL, needs-maintainer-review) — Native Rust XMPP with optional OMEMO. Marks the WeCom/WeChat/Lark channel expansion but has been waiting on maintainer review for a month.
  • #10391 companion doc PR #12403 — Composition-seam row; both need author action.

Recommendation: The needs-author-action and needs-maintainer-review XL PRs (#10391, #10412, #11847) are the project's critical path. Clearing them unblocks #9872, session ownership, and the XMPP channel respectively, and would materially improve the merge-to-open ratio (currently 2:48 today).
